title: Quantum Non-demolition Measurements As A Practical Primitive For Fault-tolerant Computation Against Biased Noise
authors: Christophe Vuillot, Diego Ruiz, J\'er\'emie Guillaud, Mazyar Mirrahimi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leveraging noise bias, where phase-flip errors dominate over bit-flips, can drastically reduce the hardware overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing approaches require bias-preserving CNOT gates whose implementation remains experimentally challenging and is provably impossible for strictly two-dimensional systems. We show that high-fidelity quantum non-demolition (QND) multi-qubit Pauli [MATH] measurements provide an equally powerful yet more accessible primitive. We demonstrate that such measurements can fully replace bias-preserving CNOT gates for compiling all operations required by bias-tailored error correction, including stabilizer measurements for repetition codes, XZZX surface codes, and LDPC codes. We propose concrete physical implementations of this primitive for two platforms: solid-state nuclear spins coupled to electron spin ancillas, and dissipatively stabilized superconducting cat qubits. Through circuit-level numerical simulations, we show that an asymmetric XZZX surface code implemented with weight-four QND [MATH] measurements achieves a phase-flip threshold of [MATH] and provides a qubit overhead reduction of up to [MATH] compared to a bias-unaware surface code at noise bias [MATH]. In the regime of very large bias, a repetition code with QND [MATH] measurements attains a threshold of [MATH] and achieves overhead comparable to that of a bias-preserving CNOT scheme, without requiring such a gate. Our results establish QND multi-[MATH] measurements as a practical and hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computation for a broad class of biased-noise platforms.
tldr: QND multi-qubit Pauli measurements can replace bias-preserving CNOT gates for fault-tolerant quantum computation with biased noise, enabling hardware-efficient error correction.
motivation: Bias-preserving CNOT gates are experimentally challenging and impossible in strictly 2D systems, motivating a more accessible primitive for biased-noise fault tolerance.
method: The authors propose using high-fidelity QND multi-qubit Pauli measurements as a primitive, and demonstrate implementations with solid-state nuclear spins and dissipative cat qubits, with circuit-level simulations of XZZX surface codes and repetition codes.
result: The XZZX surface code with weight-4 QND measurements achieves a phase-flip threshold of ~4% and qubit overhead reduction up to 60% at bias η=100; repetition code with QND measurements attains threshold ~10% and overhead comparable to bias-preserving CNOT schemes.
conclusion: QND multi-Pauli measurements provide a practical, hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computation for biased-noise platforms, without requiring bias-preserving CNOT gates.

title: Thermodynamics Of Classifiers
authors: Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Landauer principle bridges the energetic cost and information processing, showing that irreversible computation inevitably demands energy dissipation. As energy demands from computation continue to rise, approximate computing has attracted considerable attention. Approximate computing is based on the idea that energy consumption can be reduced by sacrificing computational accuracy. This raises a fundamental question about the relationship between error and thermodynamic cost in information processing. In this study, we derive the error-cost trade-off in the binary classifier by considering classification based on Markov processes. We obtain the lower bounds on the Bayes error in terms of thermodynamic costs such as entropy production and dynamical activity. Our results show that when entropy production or dynamical activity vanishes, the Bayes error reaches [MATH], equivalent to random guessing, while greater thermodynamic costs enable lower error. This establishes a fundamental trade-off between error and cost in information processing by thermodynamic systems. Because the Bayes error provides the lowest achievable error among all possible classifiers, the classification error cannot fall below the obtained bounds given the entropy production or dynamical activity. We also discuss the quantum generalization and show that the Bayes error of the quantum classifier is bounded from below by the variance of the Hamiltonian.
tldr: Derives fundamental trade-offs between thermodynamic cost (entropy production, dynamical activity) and classification error (Bayes error) for binary classifiers, with a quantum generalization linking error to Hamiltonian variance.
motivation: To understand the fundamental relationship between computational accuracy and energy consumption in approximate computing, addressing the question of how much thermodynamic cost is necessary to achieve a given error level.
method: Models binary classification as a Markov process and uses information-theoretic bounds to relate Bayes error to entropy production and dynamical activity; extends to quantum classifiers via Hamiltonian variance.
result: Lower bounds on Bayes error are derived: zero thermodynamic cost implies random guessing (error = 1/2), while higher costs allow lower error; quantum classifiers have error bounded by Hamiltonian variance.
conclusion: Establishes a fundamental error-cost trade-off in information processing, with implications for designing energy-efficient classifiers and understanding thermodynamic limits of computation.

title: Manipulation Of Information Flow And Thermodynamic Performance In Nonreciprocal Quantum Dot Information Engines
authors: Junjie Liu Hao Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum information engines leverage information as a thermodynamic resource to facilitate energy conversion. In the operation of such engines, the information flow between the working substance and the controller is pivotal, however, strategies for its efficient manipulation remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigate an autonomous information engine based on a double-quantum-dot setup, where a downstream dot coupled to two reservoirs acts as the working substance, and an upstream dot coupled to a single reservoir serves as the controller. By extending the second law of thermodynamics to incorporate the effects of nonreciprocal couplings between the dots and their electronic reservoirs, we develop a thermodynamic framework that allows us to demonstrate that nonreciprocity can significantly modulate the inter-dot information flow, thereby providing a robust control mechanism. We show that the influence of nonreciprocity can be equivalently understood through a mapping to an effective reciprocal system upon a reparameterization of chemical potentials and the electron-electron coupling strength. We further analyze the impact of nonreciprocity on the engine's performance and operation regime. Our findings establish nonreciprocal coupling as an effective control knob for designing and optimizing quantum dot information engines, surpassing the capabilities of conventional reciprocal configurations.
tldr: Nonreciprocal couplings between quantum dots and reservoirs can modulate information flow and enhance thermodynamic performance of autonomous quantum information engines.
motivation: To explore how nonreciprocity can be used to manipulate information flow in quantum dot information engines, which is crucial for optimizing energy conversion but remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamic framework extending the second law to include nonreciprocal couplings, and analyze a double-quantum-dot setup with one dot as working substance and the other as controller.
result: Nonreciprocity significantly modulates inter-dot information flow, providing a robust control mechanism; its effect can be mapped to an effective reciprocal system with reparameterized chemical potentials and coupling strength.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling serves as an effective control knob for designing and optimizing quantum dot information engines, surpassing conventional reciprocal configurations.

title: Bit Flips, Saturation, And Quantum Chaos In Dissipative Cat Qubits
authors: Filippo Ferrari, Joachim Cohen, Vincenzo Savona, Fabrizio Minganti
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bosonic cat qubits promise hardware-efficient quantum error correction because their logical bit-flip rate is exponentially suppressed with the photon number of the cat state. However, several experiments report a saturation of this suppression at large photon numbers, thus limiting the achievable protection. Combining quantum-trajectory simulations, semiclassical analysis, and Liouvillian spectral methods, we investigate the properties of bit flips in realistic dissipative cat qubits, where a memory mode hosting quantum information interacts with a dissipative buffer cavity. We show that bit flips are dynamical processes inherently involving both the memory and buffer, and therefore cannot be captured by single-mode approximate descriptions. We identify a reflection symmetry, resulting in a phase-locking condition at the semiclassical level and for quantum trajectories, as the main requirement for regular bit-flip dynamics. Its breakdown is the origin of the saturation, and we find that it occurs when two conditions are met. First, the adiabatic approximation, where the state of the buffer instantaneously follows that of the memory, must not be valid, which typically happens at large photon numbers. Second, key parameters such as the cross-Kerr interaction and dephasing must be present, leading to irregular dynamics in which memory fluctuations are amplified by the buffer during bit flips. In this regime, we find that bit flips manifest as chaotic bursts within otherwise regular dynamics, as evidenced by both changes in the topology of quantum trajectories and in the Liouvillian spectrum and its associated eigenmodes involved in these switching events. Finally, we verify our predictions against experimental data, highlighting the detrimental role of dissipative chaotic behavior in bosonic error-correcting codes.
tldr: This paper identifies the breakdown of a reflection symmetry as the origin of bit-flip saturation in dissipative cat qubits, linking it to chaotic dynamics in the memory-buffer system.
motivation: Experiments on bosonic cat qubits show that the exponential suppression of bit-flip errors saturates at large photon numbers, limiting error correction performance. The authors aim to understand the mechanism behind this saturation.
method: The study combines quantum-trajectory simulations, semiclassical analysis, and Liouvillian spectral methods to analyze bit-flip dynamics in a realistic dissipative cat qubit model with a memory mode coupled to a buffer cavity.
result: Bit flips are inherently two-mode processes; saturation occurs when the adiabatic approximation fails and cross-Kerr interaction and dephasing cause irregular, chaotic dynamics that amplify memory fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings explain experimental observations of bit-flip saturation and highlight dissipative chaos as a detrimental effect in bosonic error-correcting codes, suggesting that controlling the reflection symmetry and adiabaticity is crucial for improving cat qubit performance.

title: Bell State Analysis Provides An Optimal Basis Saturating The Quantum Cramer-Rao In Rotation Sensing
authors: Daniel F. V. James Zhuoran Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The second-order anti-coherent state of light is known to saturate the Cramer-Rao Bound (QCRB) for rotation sensing around an arbitrary axis. However, due to the complexity of the state and the inefficiency of state tomography, parameter extraction remains an open problem. In this manuscript, we approach the problem of parameter extraction using pair-wise Bell state analysis with an additional path degree of freedom. Due to the transformation property of rotation, only the symmetric Bell states will show up in projection in the final state. We exploit this advantage to develop a scheme for extracting the rotation angle for N=4 and N=6 second-order anti-coherent states.
tldr: This paper proposes a Bell state analysis scheme for extracting rotation parameters from second-order anti-coherent states, achieving the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Second-order anti-coherent states saturate the QCRB for rotation sensing but parameter extraction is challenging due to state complexity and tomography inefficiency.
method: The authors use pairwise Bell state analysis with an additional path degree of freedom, exploiting that only symmetric Bell states appear under rotation, to extract rotation angles for N=4 and N=6 anti-coherent states.
result: The scheme provides an optimal basis for rotation sensing, saturating the QCRB, and demonstrates a practical parameter extraction method.
conclusion: This work advances quantum metrology by linking Bell state analysis to optimal rotation sensing, with potential applications in quantum information and sensing.

title: Phase-resolved Multichannel Quantum Escape Between Limit Cycles
authors: Caroline Nowoczyn, Ludwig Mathey, Kilian Seibold
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven-dissipative quantum systems can recover stable dynamical attractors in the semiclassical limit, including coexisting limit cycles. At finite fluctuation strength, this classical coexistence becomes quantum metastability: the corresponding oscillatory states undergo rare fluctuation-induced transitions. We demonstrate phase-resolved quantum escape between two such states in a driven optomechanical resonator. Unlike escape from fixed points, switching between extended attractors occurs across a periodic basin boundary and depends on the phase at which fluctuations approach it. Using quantum-jump trajectories across a controlled quantum-to-classical crossover, we reconstruct the escape geometry directly from switching events. Escape from the small-amplitude cycle proceeds through a single radial corridor and exhibits near-Arrhenius scaling, whereas escape from the large-amplitude cycle involves competing phase-localized corridors with distinct effective activation scales. The resulting curvature in the switching-rate scaling, together with event-conditioned phase distributions, identifies finite-fluctuation multichannel quantum escape between extended attractors.
tldr: This paper studies phase-resolved quantum escape between limit cycles in a driven optomechanical system, revealing multichannel escape with distinct activation scales.
motivation: To understand fluctuation-induced transitions between coexisting limit cycles in driven-dissipative quantum systems, which is a fundamental aspect of nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Quantum-jump trajectory simulations across a quantum-to-classical crossover, reconstructing escape geometry from switching events.
result: Escape from small-amplitude cycle is single-channel with near-Arrhenius scaling; escape from large-amplitude cycle involves multiple phase-localized corridors with different effective activation energies, leading to curvature in switching-rate scaling.
conclusion: The work provides insights into metastability and rare events in quantum systems, with implications for understanding energy barriers and activation processes in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Quantum Differential Privacy Via Fisher Information Spectral Analysis
authors: Justice Owusu Agyemang, Jerry John Kponyo, Elliot Amponsah, Godfred Manu Addo Boakye
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) metric governs a fundamental duality: it quantifies both how precisely a parameter can be estimated (metrology) and how distinguishable two quantum states are (privacy). We exploit this duality to establish a geometry-aware framework for quantum differential privacy (DP) that replaces isotropic depolarizing noise with direction-dependent noise aligned to the QFI eigenstructure of the quantum embedding. We prove six principal theorems: (1) the minimax-optimal mechanism concentrates the noise budget in the dominant QFI eigenmode, achieving [MATH] with [MATH] advantage; (2) mixed-state QFI decomposition reveals that dephasing in the adversary's basis [MATH] accessible information, while misaligned-basis dephasing provides constructive privacy amplification from hardware noise; (3) a tight privacy [MATH] utility uncertainty relation [MATH]; (4) adaptive QFI estimation converging at [MATH] yields [MATH] tighter bounds; (5) QFI-aligned composition saturates at [MATH] versus [MATH] for standard composition; and (6) hardware noise can be harnessed for privacy amplification. Adversarial vulnerabilities, Wasserstein guarantees, subspace projection, and a zero-knowledge audit protocol follow as corollaries. Results are validated on Qiskit Aer GPU simulations, IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_fez, 156 qubits), and against classical DP baselines, achieving equivalent utility at [MATH] versus [MATH] for classical DP.
tldr: This paper introduces a geometry-aware quantum differential privacy framework that uses QFI eigenstructure to optimize noise, achieving better privacy-utility trade-offs than classical DP.
motivation: To address the suboptimal isotropic noise in quantum differential privacy by leveraging the duality between quantum metrology and privacy, and to provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for privacy in quantum algorithms.
method: The authors propose a mechanism that aligns noise with the QFI eigenstructure of the quantum embedding, prove six theorems on optimality, privacy-utility trade-offs, adaptive estimation, composition, and hardware noise amplification, and validate on Qiskit Aer GPU and IBM Quantum hardware.
result: The QFI-aligned mechanism achieves equivalent utility at epsilon=0.1 versus epsilon=1.0 for classical DP, with tighter composition bounds and constructive use of hardware noise for privacy amplification.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled way to design quantum DP mechanisms, with implications for secure quantum communication and computation, and opens avenues for further research on geometry-aware privacy in quantum systems.

title: Detectability Limits For Intra-Block Temporal Drift In Finite-Key Entanglement-Based Qkd
authors: Rafael Duarte Marcelino, Julio Smanioto Garcia, Matheus Rufino
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the statistical detectability of intra-block temporal drift in finite-key entanglement-based quantum key distribution, with particular relevance to E91-type parameter estimation and monitoring. Drift is modeled as a mean-preserving Lipschitz perturbation of Bernoulli observables, capturing structured temporal variation that is invisible to global-average tests. For a block of size [MATH] and confidence levels [MATH], we formulate a minimax hypothesis-testing problem and define the minimal detectable amplitude. We derive matching lower and upper bounds yielding [MATH]: if [MATH], no level-[MATH] procedure can guarantee nontrivial uniform power over the admissible drift class, whereas a calibrated CUSUM statistic detects drift at the matching scale. Explicit constants for linear, sinusoidal, and step profiles, together with simulations, confirm the predicted scaling collapse. The result quantifies a finite-block monitoring-resolution limit and is distinct from composable security certification.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on detecting intra-block temporal drift in finite-key entanglement-based QKD, deriving matching lower and upper bounds for the minimal detectable drift amplitude.
motivation: In entanglement-based QKD (e.g., E91 protocol), parameter estimation and monitoring rely on statistical tests that may be blind to structured temporal variations within a block. Understanding the detectability limits of such drift is crucial for practical security and system monitoring.
method: The authors model drift as a mean-preserving Lipschitz perturbation of Bernoulli observables and formulate a minimax hypothesis-testing problem. They derive lower bounds via information-theoretic arguments and upper bounds by constructing a calibrated CUSUM statistic that achieves the optimal detection scale.
result: The minimal detectable drift amplitude scales as (log(1/δ)/n)^{1/2} for block size n and confidence level δ, with explicit constants for linear, sinusoidal, and step profiles. Simulations confirm the predicted scaling collapse.
conclusion: The result quantifies a finite-block monitoring-resolution limit distinct from composable security, providing practical guidelines for parameter estimation in finite-key QKD systems.

title: Distinguishing Bohmian Contextuality From Kochen-Specker Contextuality
authors: Jan-{\aa}ke Larsson Anton Skott
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum contextuality is a concept used to describe the property of hidden-variable theory that measurement outcomes predetermined by the hidden variables depend on the measurement context. The term measurement context can have different meanings, giving rise to different flavours of quantum contextuality. The first discovered flavour is Kochen-Specker (KS) contextuality where measurement outcomes will depend on what compatible measurements are jointly performed with the selected measurement. Another flavour, here to be compared with KS contextuality, is that referred to in Bohmian mechanics where outcomes of some specific measurements are not completely specified by the model state, but depend also on specifics of the measurement device used. It has been claimed that this type of Bohmian contextuality is necessary to enable KS contextuality in a hidden variable model. In this paper we show that this is not the case. The recently proposed Contextual Ontological Model (COM) [Hindlycke and Larsson, Phys. Rev. Lett. 2022] produces KS contextual predictions but does not have the Bohmian contextuality; the outcome of every measurement allowed by COM can be predicted from the model state itself. This distinguishes Bohmian contextuality from KS contextuality, and enables individual study of the two concepts.
tldr: This paper distinguishes Bohmian contextuality from Kochen-Specker contextuality by showing that a contextual ontological model can achieve KS contextuality without Bohmian contextuality.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between two types of quantum contextuality—Bohmian and Kochen-Specker—and test the claim that Bohmian contextuality is necessary for KS contextuality.
method: The authors analyze the Contextual Ontological Model (COM) and demonstrate that it produces KS contextual predictions while the outcome of every measurement is predetermined by the model state, thus lacking Bohmian contextuality.
result: COM exhibits KS contextuality without Bohmian contextuality, disproving the necessity of Bohmian contextuality for KS contextuality.
conclusion: The two types of contextuality are distinct and can be studied individually, with implications for hidden-variable theories and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Otto Machine With $q$-deformed P\"oschl-Teller Oscillator
authors: Collins O. Edet, Norshamsuri Ali, Rosdisham Endut, O. Abah
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the impact of the potential parameters of the q-deformed modified P\"oschl-Teller potential on the thermodynamic performance of a quantum Otto cycle, where the [MATH]-deformed modified P\"oschl-Teller potential serves as the working substance. Analytical expressions for the energy spectrum and wave functions are derived, enabling a systematic investigation of heat exchange, work output, efficiency, and coefficient of performance. We show that [MATH]-deformation modifies the energy spectrum and creates distinct performance regions in the ([MATH], [MATH]) parameter space. Low ([MATH]) and high ([MATH]) favour optimal heat engine efficiency, whereas high ([MATH]) and low ([MATH]) improve refrigerator performance. The heat engine efficiency peaks in the low-([MATH]), high-([MATH]) regime. These results highlight the q-deformed modified P\"oschl-Teller potential as a versatile and tunable platform for exploring potential parameter-driven effects in quantum thermal machines.
tldr: This paper studies a quantum Otto cycle using a q-deformed modified Pöschl-Teller potential as the working substance, showing that deformation parameters can tune heat engine efficiency and refrigerator performance.
motivation: To explore how potential parameters of a q-deformed oscillator affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum thermal machines, providing a tunable platform for quantum Otto cycles.
method: Analytical derivation of energy spectrum and wave functions for the q-deformed modified Pöschl-Teller potential, then systematic calculation of heat exchange, work output, efficiency, and coefficient of performance in a quantum Otto cycle.
result: The q-deformation modifies the energy spectrum, creating distinct performance regions: low deformation and high potential range favor optimal heat engine efficiency, while high deformation and low potential range improve refrigerator performance.
conclusion: The q-deformed modified Pöschl-Teller potential is a versatile and tunable platform for quantum thermal machines, with potential parameter-driven effects that can be exploited for efficient energy conversion.

title: Code-agnostic Bosonic Noise Suppression With Hybrid Rotations
authors: Saurabh U. Shringarpure, Siheon Park, Sungjoo Cho, Yong Siah Teo, Hyukjoon Kwon, Srikrishna Omkar, Hyunseok Jeong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical-level noise on traveling bosonic modes remains a critical bottleneck for scalable quantum information processing. We show that for any single-mode bosonic code (qumode) corrupted by thermal or Gaussian displacement noise at loss rate [MATH] and amplification [MATH], a hybrid continuous-discrete-variable (CV-DV) interferometer using a single qubit ancilla and two controlled-Fourier (CF) gates sandwiching the noise channel suppresses its effects from linear to quadratic scaling. This is achieved without active error correction or destructive measurements of the encoded state, maintaining high success probabilities [MATH] when [MATH]. When supplemented with multiple ancillas, the protocol converts photon loss into coherent Fock-damping, and thermal or displacement noise into a mixture of Fock-diagonal noise. The protocol is entirely code-agnostic. For the special case of [MATH]-fold rotation-symmetric bosonic codes, it simplifies to conventional error detection and projection with [MATH] ancillas. Suppression with simple gates and few ancillas demonstrates a clear hardware-efficient advantage over previously proposed ``bypass'' schemes, where quantum information transferred to the DV ancillas is readily corrupted by ancilla noise. Finally, we extend the protocol to a qutrit DV ancilla. This demonstrates resilience to both CV noise and composite DV damping noise, achieving a truly hybrid noise suppression scheme that operates effectively even on CV encodings lacking a well-defined photon-number parity syndrome.
tldr: A hybrid CV-DV interferometer using a qubit ancilla and controlled-Fourier gates suppresses bosonic noise quadratically for any single-mode bosonic code without active error correction.
motivation: Physical noise on traveling bosonic modes limits scalable quantum information processing; existing bypass schemes are vulnerable to ancilla noise.
method: The protocol sandwiches a noise channel (thermal/Gaussian displacement) between two controlled-Fourier gates with a single qubit ancilla, converting noise into Fock-diagonal form; multiple ancillas enable coherent Fock-damping.
result: Noise suppression scales from linear to quadratic in loss rate, with high success probability for small loss; for rotation-symmetric codes it reduces to error detection with fewer ancillas.
conclusion: The scheme offers hardware-efficient noise suppression without active error correction, extends to qutrit ancillas for hybrid noise resilience, and is code-agnostic.

title: Multiple Fidelities And Joint Numerical Range
authors: Bang-Hai Wang Pei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effectiveness of entanglement detection based on multiple fidelities via the geometry of the joint separable numerical range. When all reference states are product states, we derive a necessary and sufficient criterion for such detection: either some pair of reference states has nontrivial moduli of the local inner products on both subsystems, or the orthogonal complement of the span of the reference states is completely entangled. We further show that there exist sets of reference product states for which no proper subset is effective for entanglement detection, whereas the full set is. A typical example of this phenomenon is provided by unextendible product bases. Moreover, for a pair of reference product states on a bipartite system with arbitrary local dimensions, we characterize both the joint numerical range and the joint separable numerical range, showing that the joint separable numerical range is determined solely by their local fidelities, as illustrated by a representative two-qubit example. Our results offer a systematic approach to designing effective entanglement witnesses and lay the groundwork for extensions to higher-dimensional and multipartite scenarios.
tldr: The paper uses the geometry of joint numerical ranges to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for entanglement detection via multiple fidelities, with applications to unextendible product bases.
motivation: To develop a systematic framework for designing effective entanglement witnesses using multiple reference states, overcoming limitations of single-fidelity witnesses.
method: The authors analyze the joint separable numerical range for sets of product reference states, deriving criteria based on local inner products and the structure of the orthogonal complement.
result: They show that entanglement detection is possible iff either some pair of reference states has nontrivial local inner product moduli on both subsystems, or the orthogonal complement is completely entangled. They also characterize the joint numerical range for two product states.
conclusion: The results provide a systematic approach to constructing entanglement witnesses and lay groundwork for extensions to higher dimensions and multipartite systems.

title: Quantum Sensing And Quantum Error Correction: Two Sides Of The Same Coin
authors: Daniel F. V. James Zhuoran Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology has been making amazing progress in the past decades. It is always in researchers' interest to search for new optimal states that improve parameter estimation. In this paper, we point out a connection between the code's error correcting capacity and its ability to act as a sensor. We backed our claim by providing an example that relates the Absorption emission code to the sensor state for arbitrary state rotation. It is hoped that, in building such a unified theory, one can draw inspiration from error correction to develop promising quantum sensors.
tldr: This paper establishes a formal connection between quantum error-correcting codes and quantum sensing, showing that code error-correcting capacity directly relates to its ability as a sensor.
motivation: To unify quantum error correction and quantum metrology, enabling cross-pollination of ideas between the two fields.
method: The authors provide a theoretical example linking an Absorption Emission code to a sensor state for arbitrary state rotation, demonstrating the duality.
result: They show that the error-correcting capability of a code can be reinterpreted as sensitivity to parameter estimation, providing a concrete example.
conclusion: This unified theory could inspire new quantum sensors by leveraging error correction techniques, and vice versa.

title: A Generative Pre-trained Transformer With Kerr-soliton Attention
authors: Lindell M. Williams, Yan Jin, Scott B. Papp
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems, particularly through generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs), have enabled capability-rich language models, but their operation incurs substantial costs in digital computation, memory, and data movement. Attention is a core operation in GPTs that computes context-dependent weights for input tokens. Since deep-learning models are defined by compositions of nonlinear transformations, identifying physical systems that can realize them offers a pathway to higher efficiency. Here, we introduce Kerr-soliton attention, harnessing driven-dissipative nonlinear dynamics in a resonator to realize, execute, and validate a deep-learning attention operation in physical hardware. We train a transformer language model using an analytic Kerr-soliton attention response and explore generative inference by streaming model-produced inputs through the experimental system. We observe high-fidelity agreement between the experimentally produced nonlinear weights and those predicted by the analytic Kerr-soliton model. Computation proceeds through streaming-in-time excitation of an ensemble of Kerr solitons, with inputs encoded as temporal signals that evolve under nonlinear dynamics. Our approach maps memory and compute onto the same physical dynamics, relaxing the need for intermediate digital storage and reducing data movement. This work points toward hybrid digital-physical learning systems in which Kerr solitons provide physical memory and high-bandwidth streaming nonlinear processing within deep-learning models.
tldr: This paper introduces Kerr-soliton attention, a physical implementation of the attention mechanism in GPTs using nonlinear dynamics in a resonator, aiming to reduce energy and memory costs.
motivation: The operation of large language models incurs substantial computational and energy costs, especially due to data movement. The authors seek to leverage physical nonlinear dynamics to perform attention more efficiently.
method: They use driven-dissipative Kerr solitons in a resonator to compute attention weights via streaming temporal signals, and train a transformer language model using an analytic model of this physical attention.
result: High-fidelity agreement between experimentally produced nonlinear weights and the analytic model is observed, demonstrating that physical Kerr-soliton dynamics can implement attention with reduced data movement.
conclusion: This work points toward hybrid digital-physical learning systems where Kerr solitons provide physical memory and high-bandwidth streaming nonlinear processing, potentially improving efficiency in deep learning.

title: Self-Generated Chiral Rotation In Whispering-Gallery Optomechanics
authors: Mohamed Hatifi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backscattering in whispering-gallery-mode resonators is usually a passive mode-splitting mechanism produced by a fixed defect. Here, we show that, when the backscatterer is a mechanical angular degree of freedom, the same process becomes an angular-recoil backaction channel capable of generating chirality under reciprocal driving. A localized movable scatterer coherently converts photons between clockwise and counterclockwise whispering-gallery modes, transferring angular recoil in each circulation-changing event. In a weak-scattering driven-dissipative model, reciprocal bidirectional pumping gives zero net torque at rest, but rotation Doppler-shifts the two opposite scattering rates in opposite directions. For suitable detuning, this feedback produces negative angular friction, destabilizes the nonrotating reciprocal state, and selects one of two symmetry-related steady rotations. The threshold scales inversely with the square of the WGM azimuthal index. The mechanically chiral state produces a direction-dependent weak-probe response, visible as a Doppler splitting of the backscattered spectra, turning passive WGM mode splitting into a minimal mechanism for autonomous chiral optomechanics.
tldr: This paper shows that a movable scatterer in a whispering-gallery-mode resonator can self-generate chiral rotation via backaction, turning passive mode splitting into an autonomous chiral optomechanical system.
motivation: To explore how mechanical degrees of freedom in optomechanical systems can lead to spontaneous chirality and rotation, potentially enabling new types of sensors or quantum transducers.
method: The authors develop a weak-scattering driven-dissipative model for a whispering-gallery-mode resonator with a localized movable scatterer, analyzing the dynamics of photon circulation and mechanical rotation under reciprocal pumping.
result: Reciprocal bidirectional pumping yields zero net torque at rest, but rotation Doppler-shifts scattering rates, leading to negative angular friction and spontaneous selection of a steady rotation direction. The threshold scales inversely with the square of the WGM azimuthal index.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a minimal mechanism for autonomous chiral optomechanics, with potential applications in nonreciprocal devices, sensing, and hybrid quantum systems where mechanical rotation couples to optical modes.

title: Quantum Dynamics Of Interacting Dissipative Oscillators: A Novel Scheme
authors: Fardin Kheirandish Ronak Moradi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of interacting quantum harmonic oscillators coupled to thermal reservoirs under the influence of an external driving field. In a novel theoretical scheme, we first analyze the case of two interacting oscillators, each coupled to its own thermal reservoir, with an external source applied to the first oscillator. By diagonalizing the total Hamiltonian through successive Bogoliubov transformations, we obtain explicit expressions for the oscillator energies. A key finding is that off resonance, the energy of the second oscillator grows unboundedly, whereas on resonance, it remains bounded and periodic. We then derive the Husimi functions for both oscillators and the reduced Husimi functions for initially separable coherent and number states. The shift of the Husimi function's maximum away from the origin at zero temperature confirms continuous energy gain under specific parameter conditions. An explicit formula for the reduced density matrix components in the number state basis is also provided. Finally, we generalize the model to [MATH] interacting oscillators in a thermal medium driven by a classical field. For the three-oscillator case, we show that on resonance, the energies of the first and third oscillators grow, while the energy of the second oscillator remains periodically bounded. These results offer insights into energy transfer and localization in coupled oscillator systems in thermal environments.
tldr: This paper studies energy transfer and localization in coupled dissipative quantum harmonic oscillators driven by an external field, revealing unbounded energy growth off resonance and bounded periodic behavior on resonance.
motivation: To understand energy dynamics in coupled oscillator systems in thermal environments, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and energy consumption in quantum systems.
method: The authors diagonalize the Hamiltonian via successive Bogoliubov transformations, derive Husimi functions, and compute reduced density matrix components for two and three oscillators coupled to thermal reservoirs.
result: Off resonance, the second oscillator's energy grows unboundedly; on resonance, it remains bounded and periodic. For three oscillators on resonance, the first and third gain energy while the second stays bounded.
conclusion: The results provide insights into energy localization and transfer in dissipative quantum systems, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and control of energy flow in networks.

title: On Constructing And Decoding Quantum Triorthogonal Codes
authors: Alessio Baldelli, Olai {\AA}. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes, Massimo Battaglioni
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A triorthogonal code is a binary quantum Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code defined by a triorthogonal matrix. Triorthogonal codes are a key ingredient in magic-state distillation, since they allow for transversal [MATH] gates, a non-Clifford logical operation useful for achieving universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. Their construction is challenging because it must satisfy simultaneous pairwise and triple-wise overlap constraints, as well as row-weight requirements. In this work, we study the construction and decoding of triorthogonal codes with prescribed dual-distance properties. We derive an existence criterion for even-weight triorthogonal generator matrices with a target dual minimum distance. The criterion combines triorthogonality constraints with MacWilliams identities via Krawtchouk-polynomial conditions on the dual weight distribution, yielding an integer linear programming formulation for the construction problem. We find new nontrivial triorthogonal codes that are not necessarily generated by classical triply-even codes. The decoding performance of high-distance triorthogonal codes obtained via the doubling construction is then evaluated over the dephasing channel. We compare bounded-distance decoding, belief propagation plus ordered-statistics post-processing, and a GRAND-based decoder adapted to the quantum setting, which turns out to be a promising option.
tldr: This paper presents new methods for constructing and decoding quantum triorthogonal codes, which are essential for magic-state distillation in fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Triorthogonal codes enable transversal non-Clifford gates, crucial for universal quantum computing, but their construction is challenging due to strict constraints. The research aims to find new codes and efficient decoders.
method: The authors derive an existence criterion using Krawtchouk polynomials and MacWilliams identities, formulate the construction as an integer linear programming problem, and evaluate decoding performance of high-distance codes via bounded-distance decoding, belief propagation with ordered-statistics post-processing, and a GRAND-based decoder.
result: New nontrivial triorthogonal codes not generated by classical triply-even codes are found. The GRAND-based decoder shows promising performance for the dephasing channel.
conclusion: The work advances the construction of triorthogonal codes and provides efficient decoding methods, contributing to fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.

title: Rare Events Of Small-noise Doob Conditioned Processes
authors: Francesco Coghi Iago N. Mamede
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Doob fixed-time conditioning enables the sampling of rare trajectories of Markov processes by modifying the drift so that reaching a prescribed target at a given time is guaranteed. We study the statistics of this conditioned path ensemble through the moment generating function in the weak-noise large deviation regime. Since the Doob drift is rarely available in closed form, we reinterpret the conditioned ensemble as the original process post-selected on the terminal constraint, thereby avoiding explicit construction of the Doob transform. This viewpoint then yields an optimal-control representation for the leading exponential contribution to the generating function, expressed as a variational principle with terminal boundary conditions set by the Doob end-point constraint. We illustrate the framework with two analytical examples and with an application to heat dissipation of a minimal model of biomolecular folding.
tldr: This paper studies rare trajectories of Markov processes conditioned on a terminal constraint via Doob transform, and applies the framework to heat dissipation in a biomolecular folding model.
motivation: To understand the statistics of rare events in conditioned stochastic processes, particularly when the Doob drift is not analytically available, and to connect this to thermodynamic quantities like heat dissipation.
method: The authors reinterpret the conditioned ensemble as post-selection on the terminal constraint, avoiding explicit Doob transform, and derive an optimal-control variational principle for the moment generating function in the weak-noise large deviation regime.
result: They obtain a variational principle with terminal boundary conditions set by the Doob end-point constraint, and illustrate it with two analytical examples and an application to heat dissipation in a minimal biomolecular folding model.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical way to compute rare-event statistics in conditioned processes without explicit Doob drift, with potential applications in nonequilibrium thermodynamics and biophysics.

title: Impact Of Surface Treatment On Noise In PL-Measurements Of Silicon Vacancies In 4H-SiC Lateral pin-Diodes
authors: Jannik H. Schwarberg (chair Of Electron Devices At Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg), Fabian Magerl (chair Of Electron Devices At Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg), Susanne Beuer (fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Devices Technology), Alexander May (fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Devices Technology), Christian Gobert (fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Devices Technology), Martin Siebert (department Of Energy Materials And Test Devices At Fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Device Technology), Christian Miersch (department Of Energy Materials And Test Devices At Fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Device Technology), Heino M\"oller (intego Gmbh), Wolfgang Knolle (leibniz-Institut F\"ur Oberfl\"achenmodifizierung), Chihang Luo (department Of Modern Physics, University Of Science And Technology Of China), Jan F. Dick (chair Of Electron Devices At Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg, Fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Devices Technology), Franziska C. Beyer (department Of Energy Materials And Test Devices At Fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Device Technology), Mathias Rommel (fraunhofer Institute For Integrated Systems And Devices Technology), J\"org Schulze
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon vacancies ([MATH]) in 4H-SiC are promising candidates for quantum technologies due to their long spin coherence times and integrability into mature semiconductor platforms. However, conventional CMOS-compatible processing introduces significant photoluminescence noise from passivation layers and crystal damage, degrading color center coherence and excitation linewidths. This work evaluates strategies to minimize such background noise. Thermally grown oxides with nitrogen monoxide annealing provide excellent low-noise passivation, remaining stable during subsequent [MATH] thermal treatments. Furthermore, combining reactive ion etching with atomic layer etching eliminates ion-induced surface damage. Into lateral pin-diodes, used for stark shift and photoluminescent excitation linewidth tuning, a selectively etched optical window is integrated. These devices show ideal electrical properties -- blocking up to [MATH] with leakage current below [MATH] -- while significantly enhancing the [MATH] environment. Single emitters in these pin-diodes show an increased signal-to-noise ratio of 15 for near-surface and of 50 for deeper emitters on both c-plane and a-plane wafers.
tldr: This paper investigates surface treatments to reduce photoluminescence noise from silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC pin-diodes, improving signal-to-noise ratio for quantum applications.
motivation: Silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC are promising for quantum technologies but suffer from noise due to CMOS-compatible processing. The research aims to minimize background noise to enhance color center coherence and excitation linewidths.
method: The authors evaluate thermally grown oxides with NO annealing and combine reactive ion etching with atomic layer etching to eliminate surface damage. They integrate a selectively etched optical window into lateral pin-diodes.
result: Thermally grown oxides with NO annealing provide low-noise passivation stable under thermal treatments. The combined etching eliminates ion-induced damage. Devices show ideal electrical properties and enhanced signal-to-noise ratio of 15 for near-surface and 50 for deeper emitters.
conclusion: The proposed surface treatments significantly improve the performance of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC, making them more viable for quantum technologies. Future work may focus on further optimization and integration into quantum devices.

title: Aklt State Is Indeed The Observation Process Of A Causal Hidden Quantum Markov Model
authors: Abdessatar Souissi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a rigorous formulation of the spin-1 Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki (AKLT) state within the framework of hidden quantum Markov models (HQMMs). We show that the AKLT ground state admits a natural representation as the observable output of a causal HQMM, thereby endowing it with an underlying hidden quantum memory that is fully consistent with its standard finitely correlated (matrix product state) description. This viewpoint yields a compact and structurally transparent characterization of the AKLT chain as a quantum spin system equipped with intrinsic quantum memory. Our results further indicate that the HQMM framework provides a promising setting for analyzing measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) and related information-processing tasks.
tldr: The paper reformulates the AKLT state as a hidden quantum Markov model, revealing its underlying quantum memory structure.
motivation: To provide a rigorous HQMM formulation of the AKLT state and explore its implications for measurement-based quantum computation.
method: The authors construct a causal hidden quantum Markov model that reproduces the AKLT ground state as its observable output, linking it to the matrix product state representation.
result: The AKLT state is shown to be naturally representable as the output of an HQMM, endowing it with a hidden quantum memory consistent with its finitely correlated description.
conclusion: The HQMM framework offers a compact characterization of the AKLT chain and may be useful for MBQC and quantum information processing.

title: Electrodynamics As A Theory Of Persistent Stochastic Processes
authors: Partha Ghose
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A process-theoretic approach to electrodynamics based on persistent Kac-type stochastic processes is developed. Finite-velocity stochastic propagation is taken as primary, while relativistic wave equations arise as emergent descriptions after analytic continuation of Telegrapher-type dynamics. The Dirac and Maxwell equations are interpreted as arising from closely related persistent propagation structures differing only in spin representation. The framework is not intended to modify the successful empirical predictions of quantum electrodynamics, but to provide a different underlying ontology. Particles and fields are not treated as primitive entities with fixed intrinsic properties. Instead, relativistic particle and field structures emerge as stable collective modes of coupled persistent stochastic dynamics. Mass and charge acquire interpretations respectively as persistence and stochastic coupling scales. Stationary bound states are interpreted as metastable persistent stochastic modes with nontrivial internal sector dynamics. Spontaneous emission is viewed as stochastic destabilization of such modes, while stimulated emission arises through resonant synchronization of persistent transition currents by incident radiation. Gauge interactions are introduced at the level of propagation-sector amplitudes prior to the emergence of observable probabilities. Radiative effects, including the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron, are interpreted as effective stochastic dressing of coupled matter--radiation processes. Some comments on gauge symmetry, equilibration and the Standard Model are also included.
tldr: This paper proposes a process-theoretic reinterpretation of electrodynamics based on persistent stochastic processes, deriving Dirac and Maxwell equations as emergent phenomena.
motivation: To provide an alternative ontology for electrodynamics that avoids treating particles and fields as primitive entities, instead deriving them from stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors develop a framework using persistent Kac-type stochastic processes with finite propagation velocity, and show that analytic continuation of Telegrapher-type dynamics yields relativistic wave equations.
result: Dirac and Maxwell equations emerge from closely related persistent propagation structures differing only in spin representation; mass and charge are interpreted as persistence and stochastic coupling scales; radiative effects like the anomalous magnetic moment are interpreted as stochastic dressing.
conclusion: The framework offers a different underlying ontology without modifying empirical predictions of QED, with implications for understanding gauge interactions, equilibration, and the Standard Model.

title: Fermi-Dirac Machines As Quantizations Of Neurons
authors: Alexander He, Nana Liu, Mark M. Wilde
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermi-Dirac machines were proposed recently as an approach to solving semidefinite optimization problems on quantum computers. Here, we reinterpret them as canonical quantizations of classical neurons. By viewing a classical neuron as an activation function applied to a parameterized classical Hamiltonian, we quantize this model by replacing classical variables with operators whose eigenvalues encode their possible values. This follows the standard approach to canonical quantization in quantum mechanics. Crucially, when the Hamiltonian consists of commuting operators, our construction reduces exactly to a classical neuron. More generally, our approach yields an activation observable, defined as an activation function applied to a parameterized quantum Hamiltonian. The output of this quantized neuron is a random variable with expectation value equal to that of the activation observable with respect to an input state. We develop efficient hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for evaluating outputs and gradients of our quantized neurons, enabling evaluation and training. These algorithms rely on basic primitives that include random sampling, Hamiltonian simulation, and the Hadamard test. We also quantize a whole host of other activation functions, including the smooth rectified linear unit (ReLU), sigmoid linear unit, Gaussian-smoothed ReLU, and Gaussian error linear unit (GeLU), which are known to be useful for deep learning applications. Numerical experiments indicate that neurons based on quantum Hamiltonians can learn functions that classical neurons cannot. We further define a computational decision problem based on Fermi-Dirac neurons and prove that it is BQP-complete, providing complexity-theoretic evidence against efficient classical simulation. Finally, we generalize our approach to continuous quantum variables and sketch two different ways of composing these neurons into networks.
tldr: This paper reinterprets Fermi-Dirac machines as quantized neurons and shows they can learn functions classical neurons cannot, with BQP-completeness.
motivation: To bridge quantum computing and neural networks by providing a canonical quantization of classical neurons, enabling quantum advantages in learning.
method: Canonical quantization of classical neurons by replacing classical variables with operators; hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for evaluation and training using Hamiltonian simulation and Hadamard test.
result: Quantized neurons can learn functions beyond classical capabilities; the decision problem for Fermi-Dirac neurons is BQP-complete.
conclusion: This work opens a new direction for quantum neural networks with provable quantum advantage, but practical implementation remains challenging.

title: On The Fast Fourier Transform On Su(2)
authors: Alejandro Uma\~na Julio Delgado
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The special unitary group SU(2) plays a fundamental role in the description of symmetries in quantum mechanics, theoretical physics, and spherical signal processing. In this paper, we address the computational challenges of performing spectral analysis on this non-abelian compact Lie group. We present the Fourier Transform (FT) on SU(2) and develop a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm inspired by the classical Cooley-Tukey divide-and-conquer scheme. Our approach efficiently discretizes the group using Euler angles, applying a two-dimensional FFT on the angular variables and exploiting the recursive properties of Jacobi polynomials. We provide an analysis of the computational complexity, demonstrating that our FFT-based method significantly outperforms the direct computation of the FT. This algorithm serves as a foundational tool for understanding the implementation of the FFT on SU(2), a key component in numerical simulations and advanced data analysis for high-performance computing applications on curved manifolds and quantum systems.
tldr: This paper develops a Fast Fourier Transform algorithm for the SU(2) group, improving computational efficiency for spectral analysis on this non-abelian compact Lie group.
motivation: Spectral analysis on SU(2) is computationally challenging; direct Fourier transform is inefficient. The authors aim to develop a faster algorithm inspired by the Cooley-Tukey FFT.
method: The algorithm discretizes SU(2) using Euler angles, applies a 2D FFT on angular variables, and exploits recursive properties of Jacobi polynomials.
result: The FFT-based method significantly outperforms direct computation of the Fourier transform on SU(2) in terms of computational complexity.
conclusion: This algorithm provides a foundational tool for numerical simulations and data analysis on curved manifolds and quantum systems, with potential applications in high-performance computing.

title: Supersymmetry Without Time-Reversal Invariance In Model A: A Frg Perspective
authors: Sankarshan Sahu, Bertrand Delamotte, Adam Ran\c{c}on, Matthieu Tissier
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, contrary to common belief, supersymmetry alone is not sufficient in Model A dynamics to ensure relaxation toward a stationary state satisfying time-reversal invariance (TRI). An additional condition on top of supersymmetry is required for TRI, which we analyze in detail. We explicitly construct a model that is supersymmetric but violates TRI, and argue that, at least perturbatively, TRI nevertheless emerges as an effective large-scale symmetry. Using the functional renormalization group (FRG), we further show that the dynamical effective action, [MATH], contains the derivative of the equilibrium effective action, [MATH], whose renormalization-group flow is identical to that of the equilibrium theory order by order in the derivative expansion. Finally, extending the same line of reasoning, we show that the probability distribution of the total magnetization in the Ising model can be recovered within the Model A framework.
tldr: This paper shows that supersymmetry alone does not guarantee time-reversal invariance in Model A dynamics, and uses functional renormalization group to analyze the emergence of equilibrium behavior.
motivation: To challenge the common belief that supersymmetry in Model A dynamics ensures relaxation to a time-reversal invariant stationary state, and to clarify the conditions for equilibrium.
method: The authors construct a counterexample model that is supersymmetric but violates time-reversal invariance, and analyze it using the functional renormalization group (FRG) within a derivative expansion.
result: Supersymmetry is insufficient for time-reversal invariance; an additional condition is required. However, perturbatively, time-reversal invariance emerges as an effective large-scale symmetry. The FRG flow of the dynamical effective action matches that of the equilibrium theory.
conclusion: The findings refine the understanding of supersymmetry in dynamical systems and show that equilibrium properties can be recovered within Model A, with implications for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Universal Classification Of Continuous Phase Transitions With Two Order Parameters
authors: Feng-Xiao Sun Yilun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continuous phase transition, indicated by the macroscopic order parameter and the occurrence of the spontaneous symmetry breaking, is well illustrated based on the Ginzburg-Landau's paradigm. In systems described by one order parameter, the phase diagram is only composed of the normal phase and the ordered phase. However, in systems with two or more order parameters, much richer phase diagrams and critical phenomena may emerge. According to coupling terms of the free energy, we classify the systems with two order parameters into several categories, featuring different patterns of phase diagrams and critical scalings respectively. Our work propose the new avenue to studying and evaluating the complex systems only based on the coupling terms in expressions of free energy.
tldr: This paper classifies continuous phase transitions in systems with two order parameters based on coupling terms in the free energy.
motivation: To understand the richer phase diagrams and critical phenomena that emerge in systems with multiple order parameters, beyond the standard Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.
method: The authors categorize systems with two order parameters by analyzing coupling terms in the free energy expansion, identifying distinct patterns of phase diagrams and critical scaling.
result: Several categories of systems are identified, each with characteristic phase diagrams and critical behaviors determined by the form of coupling.
conclusion: The work provides a new framework for studying complex systems based solely on free energy coupling terms, potentially guiding future experimental and theoretical studies.

title: Dynamical Self-dual Criticality In Fibonacci-monitored Quantum Ising Chains
authors: Finn Eckstein, Harald Schmid, Quinten Preiss, Simon Trebst, Felix von Oppen, Guo-Yi Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising chain, Kramers-Wannier duality not only protects its critical properties but also pinpoints the location of the phase transition. Its role in out-of-equilibrium, monitored dynamics, however, remains largely unexplored beyond time-periodic Floquet protocols where self-duality turns into a statistical average symmetry. Here we explore the emergence of dynamical self-duality in the absence of time-translation symmetry by investigating the monitored dynamics of one-dimensional Ising/Majorana chains where measurements are arranged in a quasiperiodic Fibonacci sequence. We find that the dynamical extension of this non-invertible symmetry to an out-of-equilibrium setting allows one to organize the dynamical phase diagram of entangled phases, both predicting the transition locations and protecting universal critical behavior. Analytically and numerically, we identify two distinct critical lines, both related to the golden ratio, for Born-rule weak measurements and for random Clifford projective measurements. The latter coincides with the transition of a pure imaginary-time evolution, which can be viewed as a post-selected trajectory. The universality classes of the long-time critical steady states at Fibonacci times are determined, while the transient dynamics between Fibonacci times is deformed by measurements, realizing dynamical measurement-altered quantum criticality in real time.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical self-dual criticality in monitored quantum Ising chains with Fibonacci measurement sequences, revealing two critical lines related to the golden ratio.
motivation: To explore the role of Kramers-Wannier duality in out-of-equilibrium monitored dynamics beyond Floquet protocols, specifically in the absence of time-translation symmetry.
method: Analytical and numerical study of one-dimensional Ising/Majorana chains with quasiperiodic Fibonacci measurement sequences, considering Born-rule weak measurements and random Clifford projective measurements.
result: Two distinct critical lines are identified, both related to the golden ratio, with universality classes determined for long-time critical steady states; transient dynamics exhibit measurement-altered quantum criticality.
conclusion: The work extends non-invertible symmetries to out-of-equilibrium settings, organizing dynamical phase diagrams and protecting universal critical behavior, with implications for monitored quantum dynamics and measurement-induced phases.

title: Minimally Destructive Fast Imaging Of Single Atoms In An Optical Tweezer Array With Coherent Excitation
authors: Rei Yokoyama, Takumi Kashimoto, Kosuke Shibata, Yuki Kawamura, Toshi Kusano, Chih-Han Yeh, Reiji Asano, Yuma Nakamura, Tetsushi Takano, Yosuke Takasu, Yoshiro Takahashi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultracold neutral atoms in an optical lattice and an optical tweezer array offer highly-controllable quantum many-body systems, utilized for various quantum science and technology such as quantum computing, quantum metrology, and quantum simulation. By combining high-fidelity imaging of individual atoms, one can further enhance the capability of such experimental platforms as quantum gas microscopes, tweezer clocks, and tweezer-array-based quantum computers. In this work, we propose a minimally destructive single-atom imaging by deterministic coherent excitation of atoms with alternately applied pi-pulses from counter-propagating directions, mitigating the fundamental heating effect associated with the stochastic absorption process. Using ytterbium-174 atoms trapped in an optical tweezer array, we experimentally demonstrate fast and low-loss single-atom imaging with a discrimination fidelity of 99.89(5) % and a survival probability of 98.80(44) % in 17.6 microseconds. Importantly, our scheme exhibits the lower heating rate, about half of that of the former scheme utilizing the incoherent excitation. This fast and minimally destructive imaging scheme is beneficial for relaxing the requirement on the trap depth, thereby enabling scalable atom imaging across a wide range of quantum science platforms.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fast, minimally destructive single-atom imaging technique using coherent pi-pulses in an optical tweezer array, achieving high fidelity and low heating.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum computing and simulation with optical tweezer arrays, fast and low-loss single-atom imaging is needed, but conventional methods cause heating and atom loss.
method: The authors use deterministic coherent excitation with alternating pi-pulses from counter-propagating directions to image atoms, reducing stochastic absorption heating.
result: They achieve 99.89% discrimination fidelity and 98.80% survival probability in 17.6 microseconds, with about half the heating rate of incoherent excitation.
conclusion: This imaging scheme relaxes trap depth requirements and benefits scalable atom imaging for quantum science platforms.

title: Towards Scalable Quaternary Message-Passing Decoding For Quantum Error Correction
authors: Boqing Zhang, Henry D. Pfister, Hanwen Yao, Siyuan Niu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scalability and interpretability of message-passing (MP) decoding, such as (quaternary) Belief Propagation, remain open challenges in quantum error correction. Even for surface codes, arguably the first testbed for decoding methods, studies of improved MP decoders have mostly been restricted to small distances ([MATH]). Moreover, the mismatch with established message-passing theory limits the decoder's interpretability, making it unclear whether MP decoding can sustain its effectiveness at large system sizes. This work takes a step toward a more principled and interpretable MP decoding framework, with the goal of making MP-based decoding more reliable and bridging theory and practice. We introduce a dilution method, which allows a quaternary Min-Sum (MS) decoder to exhibit an apparent depolarizing threshold of [MATH] up to distance [MATH], outperforming Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching in finite-length regimes. Notably, for [MATH]-noise, the standard MS decoder under dilution has worst-case complexity [MATH] and outperforms BP-OSD at [MATH]. The observed [MATH] threshold may correspond to a true asymptotic threshold. Finally, we give a graph-dilution argument that interprets the success of the dilution method and offers insight into when MP algorithms can genuinely scale. Taken together, these results provide encouraging progress toward scalable and interpretable MP decoding in quantum error correction.
tldr: This paper proposes a dilution method for quaternary Min-Sum decoding to improve scalability and interpretability of message-passing decoders for quantum error correction.
motivation: Message-passing decoders like Belief Propagation face scalability and interpretability challenges in quantum error correction, even for surface codes at small distances.
method: The authors introduce a dilution method that modifies the quaternary Min-Sum decoder, reducing complexity and improving threshold performance.
result: The diluted Min-Sum decoder achieves an apparent depolarizing threshold up to distance 21, outperforming Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching in finite-length regimes, and for X-noise, it has worst-case complexity O(n) and outperforms BP-OSD at distance 21.
conclusion: The results suggest that the dilution method can make MP decoding more scalable and interpretable, potentially bridging theory and practice in quantum error correction.

title: Quantum-Adaptive KS($\varphi$): A Parameterized Three-Qubit Gate Family Embedding Toffoli With Measurement-Free Phase Kickback And Intrinsic Error Non-Amplification
authors: Marek Perkowski Kripa Sankaranarayanan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Quantum-Adaptive KS([MATH]) ([MATH] = kickback, [MATH] = sandwich), a parameterized three-qubit gate family that structurally embeds the Toffoli (CCX) gate within two additional components: (1)a palindromic Hadamard sandwich on the first control qubit [MATH] that conjugates [MATH]-type errors to [MATH]-type in the CCX frame, providing simultaneous sensitivity to both error types without ancilla overhead; and (2)a controlled-phase (CP) gate whose quantum phase kickback propagates post-CCX target-state information into the control-qubit phase without measurement. The term Quantum- Adaptive refers to amplitude steering conditioned by the compile-time parameter [MATH] via a Quantum Neural Cellular Automaton (QNCA) majority-inspired bias rule; the gate does not self-modify at runtime. Two QA-KS([MATH]) gates chained on a shared control qubit [MATH] produce outputs completely orthogonal to two sequential CCX gates on [MATH]=1 inputs (output fidelity F=0.000), while agreeing exactly on [MATH]=0 inputs (F=1.000). This subspace-dependent divergence is the direct computational signature of coherent phase retention across gate boundaries -- impossible for CCX-only circuits. On the [MATH] = 0 subspace the gate acts deterministically (up to a relative phase), providing intrinsic error non-amplification. On the [MATH] = 1 subspace it produces four-component entangled superpositions, making it a strictly distinct quantum-native primitive from CCX. We present the complete [MATH] unitary matrix, confirmed exact to [MATH], and define two canonical variants: QA-KS[MATH] ([MATH], [MATH] gate) and QA-KS[MATH] ([MATH], [MATH] gate). Qiskit depolarizing-noise simulation demonstrates near-unit fidelity at [MATH] with an honest depth cost at higher error rates. The gate preserves the three-qubit footprint of CCX with no qubit overhead.
tldr: The paper introduces a parameterized three-qubit gate family that embeds the Toffoli gate with phase kickback and error non-amplification, but it is primarily a quantum computing primitive with no direct connection to the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To design a new quantum gate that improves upon the Toffoli gate by providing intrinsic error non-amplification and coherent phase retention without ancilla overhead.
method: The authors propose a gate family called QA-KS(φ) that combines a palindromic Hadamard sandwich, a controlled-phase gate, and a parameterized amplitude steering rule inspired by quantum neural cellular automata.
result: The gate family shows subspace-dependent divergence from CCX gates, achieving zero fidelity on |1⟩ inputs and exact agreement on |0⟩ inputs, with near-unit fidelity under depolarizing noise at low error rates.
conclusion: The QA-KS(φ) gate is a distinct quantum primitive that may be useful for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but its relevance to the user's specific research areas is limited.

title: Digital Twins For Compact Hybrid Quantum Classical Learning In Fmcw Radar Detection
authors: Sebastian Ratto Valderrama, Ahmed N. Sayed, Arien Sligar, Jose R. Rosas-Bustos, Omar M. Ramahi, George Shaker
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous-wave radar sensing often relies on labeled measurements that are costly, restricted, or difficult to collect at scale. This work evaluates physics-informed digital twins as controlled testbeds for early-stage quantum-classical radar learning. Two synthetic radar benchmarks are considered: unmanned aerial vehicle classification from range-Doppler maps and human fall detection from Doppler-time spectrograms. For both tasks, inputs are standardized, reduced using principal component analysis, and classified using either a radial basis function support vector classifier or a quantum support vector classifier. All quantum-kernel results are obtained using noiseless classical simulation; no quantum hardware is used, and no quantum-advantage claim is made. Across five random seeds, the quantum support vector classifier improves the UAV benchmark from four principal components onward, reaching an accuracy of 0.941 +/- 0.012 at eight components, compared with 0.880 +/- 0.029 for the classical baseline. On the fall-detection benchmark, both classifiers perform similarly, with a small quantum-kernel improvement at higher feature dimensions. A Gaussian-noise robustness study shows limited performance degradation across the tested noise levels, while preserving the UAV quantum-kernel gain. These results support digital twins as useful, controlled environments for radar-QML benchmarking prior to measured-data validation and hardware execution.
tldr: This paper evaluates digital twins for benchmarking quantum-classical hybrid machine learning in FMCW radar detection tasks, finding modest improvements with quantum kernel methods in simulation.
motivation: To address the scarcity of labeled radar data by using physics-informed digital twins as controlled testbeds for early-stage quantum-classical radar learning.
method: Two synthetic radar benchmarks (UAV classification and fall detection) are processed with PCA and classified using classical RBF SVM and quantum SVM (simulated noiselessly).
result: Quantum SVM outperforms classical SVM on UAV classification (0.941 vs 0.880 accuracy at 8 components) but shows similar performance on fall detection; robustness to Gaussian noise is demonstrated.
conclusion: Digital twins provide useful environments for radar-QML benchmarking, but no quantum advantage is claimed and hardware validation is needed.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, Lin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lasing and coherent perfect absorption (CPA) are time-reversed manifestations of non-Hermitian light-matter interactions. While exceptional points (EPs) have been extensively explored for controlling lasing dynamics, their role in the concurrent manipulation of lasing and absorption remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence of a pair of conjugate second-order EPs (EP2s) in a gain-loss-engineered Fabry-P\'erot microcavity that enables dual-state operation involving both coherent amplification and absorption. By spatially tailoring gain and loss, we realize two such EP2s: one associated with the coalescence of coupled scattering-matrix poles and the other, its conjugate, arising from the coalescence of corresponding zeros, thereby directly linking the amplifying and absorbing branches of the system. Leveraging the branch-point topology of these conjugate EP2s, we adiabatically encircle them in the gain-loss parameter space and achieve deterministic state permutation, enabling multiple reconfigurable switching schemes for the controlled generation and manipulation of threshold lasing and CPA. Notably, simultaneous encirclement of these conjugate EP2s yields a coordinated dual-state switching protocol, resulting in a frequency-matched coexistence of lasing and absorption responses within the same cavity. Our results establish an EP-based framework for unified and flexible control of lasing and absorption in non-Hermitian photonic systems.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dual-state control of lasing and absorption via conjugate exceptional points in a non-Hermitian photonic system.
motivation: To explore the role of exceptional points in concurrently manipulating lasing and coherent perfect absorption, which has been largely unexplored.
method: Spatially tailoring gain and loss in a Fabry-Pérot microcavity to realize a pair of conjugate second-order exceptional points, and adiabatically encircling them in parameter space.
result: Achieved deterministic state permutation and reconfigurable switching between lasing and absorption, including frequency-matched coexistence of both responses.
conclusion: Establishes an EP-based framework for unified control of lasing and absorption, with potential applications in non-Hermitian photonics.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Machine Learning Algorithms For Multi-Output Time-Series Forecasting At Utility Scale
authors: Mackenson Polch\'e, Varun Puram, Aditi Lal, Weronika Golletz, Joan \'etude Arrow, Vardaan Sahgal, Kumar Ghosh, Giorgio Cortiana, Corey O'meara
