abstract: ArXiv:2605.24252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-output time-series forecasting in energy systems is challenging because of nonlinear dynamics, multi-scale seasonality, and strong dependencies across correlated series. In this work, we investigate two hybrid quantum-classical frameworks for multi-stream time-series forecasting on a real Smart Meter dataset comprising 103 household electricity consumption time-series, with experiments executed on the [MATH] superconducting quantum processor. The first model, Kernelized Quantum Reservoir Computing with Repeated Measurement (KQRC-RM), combines coupled quantum reservoirs, ancilla-assisted repeated measurement, and kernelized readouts to model temporal dynamics and cross-stream correlations jointly. For a 3-stream time-series input and output, the KQRC-RM model using 114 qubits achieves an MAE of 0.0811 on MPS simulator (36.92\% improvement over its classical analog) whereas performance degrades to an MAE of 0.1524 on hardware. The second, a Projected Quantum Kernel Gaussian Process (QGP), replaces fidelity-based kernels with projected kernels constructed from local reduced-state statistics. Using a topology-aware 100-qubit QGP model to predict 100 multi-output time-series values, we observe 49\% of time-series outputs achieve high-accuracy predictions (MAE [MATH]), with an average MAE of [MATH] for this low-error group. The medium-error regime (MAE [MATH]-[MATH]) has an average MAE of [MATH], while the high-error regime (MAE [MATH]) has an average MAE of [MATH]. Overall, this reduces the average MAE relative to the classical GP baseline by 62.01\% on MPS simulator and 40.37\% on hardware. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of hybrid quantum machine learning for multi-input, multi-output time-series forecasting at the 100+ qubit scale on NISQ devices.
tldr: This paper explores hybrid quantum-classical machine learning for multi-output time-series forecasting in energy systems, using quantum reservoir computing and projected quantum kernel Gaussian processes on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Multi-output time-series forecasting in energy systems is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and cross-series dependencies; classical methods may be insufficient, and quantum approaches could offer advantages.
method: Two hybrid models are proposed: Kernelized Quantum Reservoir Computing with Repeated Measurement (KQRC-RM) and Projected Quantum Kernel Gaussian Process (QGP). Experiments are performed on a real smart meter dataset using a superconducting quantum processor.
result: KQRC-RM achieves MAE 0.0811 on simulator (36.92% improvement over classical) but degrades to 0.1524 on hardware. QGP reduces average MAE by 62.01% on simulator and 40.37% on hardware relative to classical GP baseline.
conclusion: The results demonstrate feasibility of hybrid quantum ML for multi-output time-series forecasting at 100+ qubit scale on NISQ devices, but hardware performance still lags behind simulators.

title: Resonant Interactions In The $\alpha$-FPUT Lattice With Site-dependent Coefficients
authors: Lorenzo Migliorelli, Giovanni Dematteis, Sergio Chibbaro, Miguel Onorato
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The wave turbulence framework has proven to be an effective tool for analyzing certain features of nonlinear energy transfer in one-dimensional nonlinear chains. In this work, we extend this approach to the [MATH]-FPUT problem when the spring stiffness [MATH] and the nonlinear coefficient [MATH] are site-dependent. Although three-wave interactions are non-resonant for constant coefficients, their spatial modulation gives rise to a non-trivial resonant manifold. In this framework, we derive a new kinetic equation that suggests the possibility of substantially faster thermalization with respect to the constant coefficient case. The new kinetic equation includes also an extra term that can be associated to the Bragg-scattering mechanism, which promotes the isotropization of the wave-action spectral density function.
tldr: This paper studies resonant interactions in a site-dependent α-FPUT lattice, deriving a kinetic equation that predicts faster thermalization due to spatial modulation.
motivation: To understand how spatial inhomogeneity affects nonlinear energy transfer and thermalization in one-dimensional chains, extending wave turbulence theory to site-dependent coefficients.
method: The authors extend the wave turbulence framework to the α-FPUT lattice with site-dependent spring stiffness and nonlinear coefficient, deriving a new kinetic equation that includes Bragg-scattering terms.
result: Spatial modulation of coefficients creates a non-trivial resonant manifold for three-wave interactions, leading to a kinetic equation with an extra term that promotes isotropization and faster thermalization.
conclusion: The work suggests that inhomogeneous nonlinear chains can thermalize faster than homogeneous ones, with implications for energy transport in disordered systems.

title: Effective Skyrmion Number For Mixed Polarization States Of Light
authors: \'angel S. Sanz Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polarization skyrmions are usually characterized through a unit Stokes vector field, which defines a map from the transverse plane to the Poincar\'e (Bloch) sphere and allows one to assign a skyrmion number under appropriate boundary conditions. This description assumes complete polarization. In many optical situations, however, the local polarization state is partially polarized and is therefore described by a spectral polarization matrix rather than by a single Jones vector. We formulate a density-matrix-based effective extension of the skyrmion-number construction for statistically stationary, quasi-monochromatic paraxial fields in terms of the normalized spectral polarization matrix. Its eigenvectors define two orthogonal polarization eigenstates, corresponding to antipodal points on the sphere, while the eigenvalue imbalance is fixed by the local degree of polarization \(P({\bf r})\). Averaging the opposite skyrmion-density contributions of these two eigenpolarizations leads to an effective skyrmion number in which the usual pure-state density is weighted by \(P({\bf r})\). The resulting quantity reduces to the conventional skyrmion number for fully polarized fields and vanishes in locally unpolarized regions. In general it is not an integer topological invariant; rather, it is an integrated effective measure, constructed from local Stokes parameters, of the skyrmionic content associated with the polarized part of a mixed optical field. We illustrate the construction with an analytic Gaussian-beam example in which a degree-one polarization texture is combined with a radially varying degree of polarization.
tldr: The paper extends the concept of skyrmion number to partially polarized light using a density-matrix approach, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To generalize the skyrmion number, a topological invariant for fully polarized light, to partially polarized fields where the polarization state is mixed.
method: Uses the spectral polarization matrix to define two orthogonal eigenpolarizations and weights their skyrmion densities by the local degree of polarization.
result: The effective skyrmion number is not an integer topological invariant but an integrated measure that reduces to the conventional number for fully polarized fields and vanishes for unpolarized regions.
conclusion: Provides a tool to characterize skyrmionic content in mixed polarization states, with potential applications in optical skyrmion research.

title: A Matched Spectral Benchmark Of Quantum Inspired Feature Maps
authors: Toheeb Ogunade, Taofeek Kassim, Etinosa Osaro
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum machine learning is often motivated by the idea that quantum systems can expose useful high-dimensional structure that is difficult to access with classical models. We isolate one central component of this claim: the fixed data-encoding map. Amplitude, angle, and basis encoding are evaluated as deterministic feature maps for classical supervised learning under matched output dimensionality and strong classical controls. The benchmark compares these encodings against raw linear models, random Fourier features, polynomial features, PCA, RBF SVMs, and shallow neural networks across diverse classical datasets. Rather than treating performance as a single endpoint, we analyze the geometry of each representation through effective rank, condition number, centered kernel alignment, predictive performance, and practical overhead. The resulting picture is mechanistic: amplitude encoding can remove magnitude information through unit-sphere normalization, angle encoding can become geometrically redundant with raw linear features, and basis encoding can impose a binary Hamming geometry that is poorly aligned with smooth decision structure. These findings do not argue against quantum computation, however, they show that fixed quantum-inspired encoding geometry alone is not a reliable source of machine-learning advantage on classical data.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum-inspired feature maps (amplitude, angle, basis encoding) for classical supervised learning and finds no inherent advantage over classical methods.
motivation: To isolate whether fixed quantum-inspired data-encoding maps provide a machine-learning advantage on classical data, independent of quantum computation.
method: The authors compare amplitude, angle, and basis encoding against classical models (linear, random Fourier features, polynomial features, PCA, RBF SVM, shallow neural networks) on diverse datasets, analyzing geometry via effective rank, condition number, centered kernel alignment, predictive performance, and overhead.
result: Amplitude encoding loses magnitude information, angle encoding is geometrically redundant with raw linear features, and basis encoding imposes a binary Hamming geometry poorly aligned with smooth decision boundaries; none provide a reliable advantage.
conclusion: Fixed quantum-inspired encoding geometry alone is not a reliable source of machine-learning advantage on classical data, but this does not argue against quantum computation.

title: Local Impurity Induced Growth And Scrambling In Clean Free Fermions
authors: Qucheng Gao, Vikram Ravindranath, Xiao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study impurity-induced particle growth and scrambling in clean one-dimensional free-fermion systems. We show that a single local impurity can act as a branching source: particle or operator weight propagates coherently into the free bulk, returns to the impurity, and is locally converted into additional degrees of freedom. We develop this branching picture in three complementary settings: a monitored free-fermion model with feedback, a fully unitary interacting particle model, and Heisenberg operator dynamics with an interacting impurity. In the monitored model, we find a feedback-driven transition for both boundary and bulk impurities. In the unitary particle and operator models, a boundary impurity gives rise to an analogous transition from saturation to sustained growth and scrambling. These results reveal how a single impurity can generate complex many-body dynamics in an otherwise clean and free quantum system.
tldr: A single impurity in a clean free-fermion system can induce particle growth and scrambling via a branching mechanism, leading to transitions in monitored and unitary models.
motivation: To understand how local impurities can generate complex many-body dynamics in otherwise integrable systems, potentially bridging free and chaotic behavior.
method: Analytical and numerical study of three models: a monitored free-fermion model with feedback, a unitary interacting particle model, and Heisenberg operator dynamics with an interacting impurity.
result: A local impurity acts as a branching source, causing coherent propagation and conversion of particle/operator weight, leading to feedback-driven transitions from saturation to sustained growth and scrambling.
conclusion: Single impurities can seed complex dynamics in clean free systems, offering insights into quantum chaos and information scrambling, with potential implications for quantum control and thermalization.

title: Performance Limits Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Error Correction Schemes
authors: Lorenzo Valentini, Diego Forlivesi, Marco Chiani
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for realizing scalable quantum computation. However, when evaluating its benefits, most analyses assume idealized components, overlooking the imperfections inherent in realistic fault-tolerant (FT) implementations. In this paper, we investigate the performance of QEC schemes taking into account that quantum gates and measurements are themselves error-prone. We derive bounds for the failure probability of Shor-style FT-QEC schemes using limited structural information, such as the number of flag qubits and quantum gates. Our analysis separates and quantifies two key contributors to the failure rate: decoding errors and residual errors arising from circuit-level faults. The derived bounds highlight fundamental limitations in Shor-style FT-QEC performance and quantify how circuit imperfections degrade error correction capabilities, under the assumption of depolarizing noise.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental performance limits for Shor-style fault-tolerant quantum error correction schemes under depolarizing noise, quantifying how circuit imperfections degrade error correction.
motivation: Most QEC analyses assume idealized components, but realistic fault-tolerant implementations have error-prone gates and measurements. This work aims to understand the fundamental limitations of Shor-style FT-QEC.
method: The authors derive bounds for the failure probability of Shor-style FT-QEC using limited structural information (number of flag qubits, quantum gates) and assuming depolarizing noise. They separate decoding errors and residual errors from circuit-level faults.
result: The bounds highlight fundamental limitations in Shor-style FT-QEC performance and quantify how circuit imperfections degrade error correction capabilities.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the performance limits of fault-tolerant QEC, but the paper is primarily focused on quantum error correction rather than the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems.

title: Implicit Binarization Via Complex Phase Dynamics In Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Khen Cohen, Mark Glass, Meir Feder, Yaron Oz
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a physics-inspired continuous relaxation framework that yields substantially improved solutions for NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, including Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), binary sparse coding, and planted-solution Ising models. By parameterizing discrete binary variables as continuous wave-like states on the complex unit circle, we inherently smooth highly non-convex energy landscapes. We show that representing binary variables as complex phases reveals an implicit regularization mechanism that promotes convergence toward discrete states. Extracting this mechanism yields significant improvements even within standard real-valued optimization frameworks, using this regularizer explicitly. Empirically, this regularization yields vastly higher ground-state convergence rates than standard real-valued alternatives. Our models achieved zero error in large-scale 160x160 QUBO tasks under severe noise (sigma=0.25), and outperformed traditional algorithms (OMP and LASSO) in underdefined sparse coding with perfect recovery at sigma=0.15. The solver's robustness was further validated by recovering exact ground-state configurations in 8 out of 11 rigorously engineered planted-solution benchmarks.
tldr: A continuous relaxation using complex phases improves combinatorial optimization by smoothing energy landscapes and implicitly binarizing variables.
motivation: To solve NP-hard binary optimization problems more effectively by avoiding poor local minima in highly non-convex landscapes.
method: Binary variables are parameterized as continuous complex phases on the unit circle, and an implicit regularization mechanism is extracted and applied to standard real-valued optimization.
result: The method achieves zero error on large QUBO tasks under noise, outperforms OMP and LASSO in sparse coding, and recovers ground states in planted-solution benchmarks.
conclusion: The complex-phase regularization offers a robust and efficient approach for combinatorial optimization, with potential extensions to other NP-hard problems.

title: Strong Eigenstate Thermalization From Mean-Ergodic Non-chaotic Dynamics
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit, Harshit Sharma, Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an example of a many-body system, derived from the double kicked top (DKT), with non-chaotic yet mean-ergodic dynamics that displays eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) in the quantum regime. The analysis addresses a key open question: whether ETH is a quantum analog of ergodicity (or mean-ergodicity). Despite non-chaotic dynamics, the fluctuations of the diagonal matrix elements of an observable scale as [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the Hilbert space dimension. Furthermore, the off-diagonal matrix elements show Gaussian statistics together with a smooth function [MATH] that becomes nearly uniform in the large-[MATH] domain. Our findings show that even mean-ergodic and non-chaotic systems can exhibit ETH.
tldr: This paper shows that eigenstate thermalization can occur in a non-chaotic, mean-ergodic many-body system, challenging the link between chaos and ETH.
motivation: To investigate whether eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) requires quantum chaos or can arise from mean-ergodicity alone.
method: The authors study a double kicked top model with non-chaotic dynamics, analyzing diagonal and off-diagonal matrix elements of observables and their fluctuations.
result: They find that diagonal matrix element fluctuations scale as 1/√D (D = Hilbert space dimension) and off-diagonal elements follow Gaussian statistics with a smooth function f(ω) becoming uniform for large D, indicating ETH.
conclusion: ETH can emerge from mean-ergodic, non-chaotic dynamics, suggesting that ETH is a quantum analog of mean-ergodicity rather than chaos.

title: Single-Chord Augmentation Of Weighted Cycles For Algebraic Connectivity And Network Coherence
authors: Jiarong Deng, Liu Chang, Quanshun Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ring-like communication graphs appear in UAV formations, cyclic patrols, perimeter monitoring, and other multi-agent tasks in which agents exchange information mainly with neighboring vehicles along a closed route. When measurement and actuation noise are persistent, a useful augmentation should improve both the convergence rate of consensus and the steady-state disagreement level. This paper studies the addition of a single weighted chord to a connected weighted cycle. The central observation is that a chord is not just a generic rank-one edge update: it splits the cycle into two complementary resistance arcs, and this resistance split governs both the algebraic-connectivity gain and the Kirchhoff-index reduction. We first derive exact chord-induced effective-resistance and Kirchhoff-index update formulas, giving a closed-form coherence objective. We then prove that, under bounded conductances and small resistance discrepancy, near-antipodal resistance-balanced chords are near-optimal for algebraic-connectivity improvement; an i.i.d. bounded-conductance model yields the same conclusion with high probability. Finally, because the best convergence-rate chord and the best coherence chord need not coincide, we formulate the design as a finite Pareto problem and introduce RBAPS and AW-RBAPS, two resistance-balanced screening rules that retain only linear or near-linear candidate sets. Numerical experiments show that AW-RBAPS remains effective beyond the formal moderate-heterogeneity regime and approximates the exhaustive Pareto front with mean hypervolume ratio [MATH] while evaluating about [MATH] of admissible chords.
tldr: This paper studies the addition of a single weighted chord to a weighted cycle graph to improve algebraic connectivity and network coherence for multi-agent consensus.
motivation: To enhance both convergence rate and steady-state disagreement in ring-like communication networks (e.g., UAV formations) under persistent noise.
method: Derives exact formulas for effective resistance and Kirchhoff index update due to a chord, then proposes resistance-balanced screening rules (RBAPS, AW-RBAPS) to approximate the Pareto front of chord placements.
result: Near-antipodal resistance-balanced chords are near-optimal for algebraic connectivity under bounded conductances; AW-RBAPS approximates the exhaustive Pareto front with high efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for augmenting cycle graphs with a single chord, but its focus on graph theory and consensus algorithms is far from the user's quantum information and thermodynamics interests.

title: Optimal Drift Optimizer For Non-convex Optimization
authors: Qin Li, Sixu Li, Eitan Tadmor, Emmanuel Tr\'elat
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a finite-horizon stochastic control criterion for non-convex optimization in which Brownian exploration is balanced against a quadratic control cost. Rather than emphasizing the classical Hopf--Cole representation, we isolate the exact drift selected by the criterion and reorganize it in a form adapted to optimization. The key object is the conditional terminal law of the optimal process. We show that this law is a Gibbs measure for a proximally penalized energy, yielding three exact representations of the drift: potential, averaged-gradient, and barycentric. We then analyze two asymptotic regimes relevant for optimization. As terminal time is approached, the drift recovers a scaled gradient-descent field. In the low-temperature regime, assuming a unique global minimizer, the conditional terminal law concentrates on it even in the presence of nonglobal local minima, and the drift converges to an affine attraction field toward it. In the nondegenerate case we also derive Laplace asymptotics for the drift, the value function, and the covariance of the conditional terminal law. Finally, we record a simple gradient-free discretization suggested by the barycentric formula.
tldr: This paper studies a stochastic control approach for non-convex optimization, deriving exact drift representations and asymptotic behaviors.
motivation: To develop a principled optimizer for non-convex problems by balancing Brownian exploration with quadratic control cost.
method: Uses finite-horizon stochastic control theory, deriving the conditional terminal law as a Gibbs measure and analyzing drift representations (potential, averaged-gradient, barycentric).
result: The drift recovers scaled gradient descent near terminal time; in low-temperature regime, it concentrates on global minimizer; Laplace asymptotics derived for nondegenerate case.
conclusion: Provides theoretical foundations for a gradient-free discretization and insights into stochastic optimization dynamics.

title: Lifted Schr\"odinger Bridges For Gaussian Mixture Endpoints: Projection Gaps And Path-Space Obstructions
authors: Siddhartha Ganguly, George Rapakoulias, Panagiotis Tsiotras
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stochastic density control between Gaussian-mixture endpoint distributions under Brownian prior dynamics. Since the direct Schr\"odinger bridge between Gaussian mixtures is generally not available in closed form, we introduce a lifted path-space construction in which each trajectory is augmented with a source--target component label. Consequently, the problem decomposes into Gaussian component-to-component Schr\"odinger bridges with explicit marginal, drift, and cost formulas, while the mixture-level assignment reduces to a finite-dimensional entropic coupling problem with a Sinkhorn scaling form. We then analyze the projection obtained by discarding or forgetting the label. By construction, the projected law satisfies the original Gaussian-mixture endpoint constraints, but its relative entropy generally differs from the lifted relative entropy by a nonnegative conditional label-information gap. This gap reveals a path-space obstruction: the lifted optimizer cannot, in general, be identified with the direct unlabeled Schr\"odinger bridge after projection. We also derive the posterior-averaged Markov drift associated with the projected marginal flow, prove a kinetic-energy upper bound, and identify a common path-potential condition under which the projection gap vanishes. Several numerical illustrations showing density and shape control are recorded for a self-contained exposition.
tldr: The paper studies lifted Schrödinger bridges for Gaussian mixture endpoints, focusing on projection gaps and path-space obstructions, with no direct connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: To address the lack of closed-form Schrödinger bridges for Gaussian mixture distributions by introducing a lifted path-space construction.
method: Augments trajectories with source-target component labels, decomposing the problem into Gaussian component-to-component bridges and a finite-dimensional entropic coupling solved via Sinkhorn scaling.
result: The projected law satisfies endpoint constraints but has a relative entropy gap due to conditional label information; a path-potential condition is identified for vanishing gap.
conclusion: The lifted optimizer generally differs from the direct unlabeled bridge, highlighting fundamental obstructions; numerical examples illustrate density control.

title: Polynomial Context-Truncation Sensitivity In Autoregressive Language Models: Sequential Wyner-Ziv Bounds For Kv Cache Compression
authors: Munsik Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rate-distortion limits of online KV cache compression in autoregressive language models, formulating it as sequential Wyner-Ziv source coding on the filtration induced by the model, with the next-step query as decoder side information. Empirically, across four models spanning two families and [MATH]-[MATH]B parameters, we find that the next-token distribution's sensitivity to context truncation decays rather than : a power law improves on an exponential fit by an order of magnitude in extrapolation, the fitted exponent is recovered independently from a sink-plus-recent KL measurement, and the decay is verified to be free of positional-encoding artifacts by a position-preserving ablation. Under a corresponding assumption, our main result characterizes the per-token memory requirement of cache policies: a sliding-window scheme attains distortion [MATH] with window [MATH], and -- under an additional two-sided Bayes-risk condition -- a converse shows [MATH] is necessary within this policy class, so the scaling is [MATH] for suffix-only policies. Whether recurrent or propagating cache summaries can beat this scaling is left open. An explicit block-Markov scheme achieves the upper bound; its rate-of-convergence exponent matches the converse under additional forward-decay and regularity hypotheses (not implied by truncation sensitivity alone), and differs by a factor of two otherwise. Empirically, the polynomial law predicts the degradation curves of concrete cache policies: recency-based eviction (sliding, sink-plus-recent) suppresses distortion by roughly two orders of magnitude over random retention at equal budget, with a power-law decay in the budget.
tldr: This paper studies the rate-distortion limits of KV cache compression in autoregressive language models using sequential Wyner-Ziv source coding, finding that context truncation sensitivity decays as a power law.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of KV cache compression in large language models, which is crucial for reducing memory usage during inference.
method: Formulates KV cache compression as sequential Wyner-Ziv source coding with next-step query as side information; empirically fits power-law decay of sensitivity to context truncation across multiple models; derives theoretical bounds for sliding-window and suffix-only cache policies.
result: Next-token distribution sensitivity to context truncation decays as a power law, not exponential; sliding-window schemes achieve distortion scaling as O(1/window) and a converse shows this is optimal for suffix-only policies; power-law predicts degradation of concrete cache policies.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical and empirical foundations for KV cache compression, but the connection to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Stochastic Compliance/evasion Dynamics In Tax Models: A Piecewise Deterministic Markov Process Approach
authors: Jonas Mayr, Amira Meddah, Irene Tubikanec
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a novel stochastic framework for modelling tax evasion dynamics by extending the deterministic model of Bertotti and Modanese (2018) through the use of Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes (PDMPs). A key limitation of the original model is the static treatment of taxpayer compliance and evasion behaviour. We address this limitation by incorporating two stochastic mechanisms:(i) audits, where random enforcement events shift non-compliant individuals toward compliance, and (ii) imitation, where social influence drives compliant individuals toward evasion. We develop each mechanism as a separate PDMP, proving that both preserve the fundamental conservation laws of population and global income. Numerical simulations show that these mechanisms produce opposing long-term outcomes: pure audits lead to full compliance, while pure imitation leads to full evasion. The central contribution is a combined PDMP model in which both dynamics interact. This model no longer converges to an extreme equilibrium state. Instead, it can exhibit persistent fluctuations around the deterministic trajectory and suggests convergence to a stationary distribution, providing a more realistic representation of compliance-evasion dynamics observed in real economies. The proposed framework offers a versatile approach for integrating behavioural stochasticity into socio-economic models.
tldr: This paper models tax evasion dynamics using Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes, extending a deterministic socio-economic model with stochastic audits and imitation.
motivation: To address the static treatment of taxpayer compliance/evasion in existing models by introducing stochastic mechanisms that better reflect real-world dynamics.
method: Two separate PDMPs for audits and imitation are developed, then combined into a single PDMP model; numerical simulations explore long-term behavior.
result: Pure audits lead to full compliance, pure imitation leads to full evasion, but the combined model exhibits persistent fluctuations and suggests convergence to a stationary distribution.
conclusion: The framework offers a versatile approach for integrating behavioral stochasticity into socio-economic models, but is not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Polarization-Induced Beam Bending: Mathematical Model, Discretization, And Algorithm
authors: Harbir Antil, Rainald L\"ohner, Sarswati Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a reduced hydrodynamic formulation of paraxial vector beam propagation in which the beam intensity, optical phase, and spatially-dependent polarization are coupled through a nonlinear dispersive system. While prior analytical work derived a solution for the beam path valid for short propagation distances, a fully resolved numerical treatment of the model over long ranges has not previously been available. Here we present a conservative numerical scheme for the coupled system, combining a finite-volume discretization of the intensity equation with monotone Hamilton--Jacobi (H-J) solvers for the phase dynamics and upwind transport of polarization. The method preserves the nonnegativity of the intensity and remains stable under long-distance propagation. We perform large-scale simulations over propagation distances of tens of meters, while resolving millimeter-scale transverse structure. The numerical results reproduce the analytically predicted and experimentally observed quadratic beam bending at short distances and reveal systematic deviations beyond the asymptotic regime. These deviations arise from nonlinear phase accumulation and dispersive effects captured by the full model but are neglected in the short-distance approximation.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical scheme for simulating polarization-induced beam bending in paraxial vector beam propagation, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Prior analytical work only provided short-distance solutions; a long-range numerical treatment was lacking.
method: A conservative numerical scheme combining finite-volume discretization for intensity, monotone Hamilton-Jacobi solvers for phase, and upwind transport for polarization.
result: Simulations over tens of meters reproduce quadratic beam bending at short distances and reveal deviations due to nonlinear phase accumulation and dispersion at long distances.
conclusion: The full model captures effects neglected in short-distance approximations, enabling accurate long-range beam propagation simulations.

title: Human-AI Collaboration In Science At Scale: A Global Large-scale Randomized Field Experiment
authors: Binglu Wang, Weixin Liang, Jiahui Xue, Yuhui Zhang, Hancheng Cao, Dashun Wang, Yian Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collaboration is the defining mode of modern science, yet its core mechanism -- feedback -- remains hard to observe, difficult to scale, and unequally distributed. Here we test whether large language models (LLMs) can contribute to this hidden but vital practice and reallocate scientific feedback, an essential yet scarce resource for knowledge production. In a global large-scale randomized field experiment, we delivered customized LLM-generated feedback for over 31,000 arXiv preprints across 150 fields and more than 45,000 researchers from 133 geographic regions. Relative to controls, authors who received feedback had a significantly higher likelihood of revising their manuscripts, corresponding to a 12.55% relative increase over the baseline revision rate. Exposure to AI feedback also increased authors' subsequent use of LLM tools in their future papers, suggesting longer-run shifts in scientific practice. These effects were strongest among authors from non-English-dominant research regions, manuscripts less embedded in the scholarly literature, and teams with lower h-indexes and earlier career stages, consistent with the idea that AI feedback may provide the greatest benefit where access to timely critique is otherwise limited. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that structured AI-based interventions can transform access to scientific feedback from a largely private advantage into a more widely distributed resource, with broader implications for productivity, equity, and capacity across the global research system.
tldr: A large-scale field experiment shows that LLM-generated feedback on arXiv preprints increases revision rates and subsequent LLM use, especially for underrepresented researchers.
motivation: To test whether LLMs can democratize access to scientific feedback, which is a scarce and unequally distributed resource.
method: Randomized field experiment delivering customized LLM feedback to over 31,000 arXiv preprints across 150 fields, with control group comparison.
result: Authors receiving AI feedback had a 12.55% relative increase in manuscript revision likelihood and increased subsequent LLM tool usage, with strongest effects for non-English-dominant regions, less embedded manuscripts, and lower-h-index teams.
conclusion: Structured AI-based interventions can transform scientific feedback from a private advantage into a widely distributed resource, improving productivity and equity.

title: Second-Order Nonlinear Response In Centrosymmetric Hyperbolic Media
authors: Evgenii E. Narimanov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that centrosymmetric natural hyperbolic media such as hexagonal boron nitride exhibit a bulk second-order nonlinear response, leading to second-harmonic and sum- and difference-frequency generation with efficiencies comparable to those of established nonlinear optical crystals such as potassium dihydrogen phosphate.
tldr: This paper shows that centrosymmetric hyperbolic media like hBN can exhibit bulk second-order nonlinear optical response, enabling efficient frequency conversion.
motivation: To challenge the conventional wisdom that second-order nonlinearity requires non-centrosymmetric materials, and to explore hyperbolic media for nonlinear optics.
method: Theoretical analysis using nonlinear optics formalism applied to hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hexagonal boron nitride.
result: Centrosymmetric hyperbolic media can have a bulk second-order nonlinear response due to the unique dispersion of hyperbolic polaritons, with efficiencies comparable to standard nonlinear crystals like KDP.
conclusion: This opens up new possibilities for nonlinear optical devices using naturally occurring hyperbolic materials, potentially simplifying fabrication and integration.

title: Dynamic Coherent Diffractive Imaging Using Only A Support Constraint In The Complex Plane
authors: Yaocheng Tian, Taichi Tsuchiya, Yu-Chen Karen Chen-Wiegart, Horacio D. Espinosa, Yuichiro Kunai, George Barbastathis
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a bounded temporal increment prior on the sample dynamics is sufficient to reconstruct a time-varying phase object from a near-field diffraction movie, under the thin-film approximation. The time evolution of the field is parameterized by a multiplicative inter-frame update factor, and a bound on its complex-plane support enforces a bounded phase increment and a passive amplitude constraint. Reconstruction of the dynamic field is thereby converted into a feasibility problem with two projection operators: a measurement-domain modulus projection and an object-domain circular-sector projection. We validate the approach experimentally using a spatial light modulator as a calibrated dynamic sample in two cases: a reaction--diffusion phase pattern with spatially expanding extent, and a growing phase pattern whose accumulated phase reaches [MATH]. In both cases the reconstructed phase trajectory agrees well with the ground truth. We then apply the same framework, without modification, to in-situ monitoring of a photo-polymer 3D printing process, recovering the spatiotemporal phase induced by polymerization under a spatially patterned blue light. The reconstructed phase trajectory provides an observable for photo-chemical system identification and process control.
tldr: This paper presents a dynamic coherent diffractive imaging method using only a support constraint in the complex plane for time-varying phase objects.
motivation: To enable reconstruction of dynamic phase objects from near-field diffraction movies without prior knowledge of the dynamics, using only a bounded temporal increment prior.
method: The time evolution is parameterized by a multiplicative inter-frame update factor with a bound on its complex-plane support, converting the reconstruction into a feasibility problem with modulus and circular-sector projections.
result: The method was validated experimentally on a spatial light modulator for reaction-diffusion and growing phase patterns, and applied to in-situ monitoring of photo-polymer 3D printing, recovering spatiotemporal phase induced by polymerization.
conclusion: The approach provides a new observable for photo-chemical system identification and process control, with potential for broader application in dynamic imaging.

title: Streaming Molecular Dynamics Simulation Data For On-the-fly Processing And Analysis
authors: Amruthesh Thirumalaiswamy, Lawson J. Woods, Heekun Cho, Hugo Macdermott-Opeskin, Jennifer Clark, Irfan Alibay, Yuxuan Zhuang, Oliver Beckstein, Matthias Heyden
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Only a small fraction of the data generated in state-of-the-art all-atom multi-microsecond molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is typically analyzed. With femtosecond integration steps, microsecond simulations generate billions of time steps containing atomic positions, velocities, and forces, often corresponding to petabytes of data. Since this exceeds practical storage capacities, only a subset of frames is usually written to trajectory files at intervals of 10-100 ps. While sufficient for ensemble averages and slow dynamics, this approach discards information on fast processes such as molecular vibrations, solvent dynamics, short-lived transition states, and transport phenomena that are directly related to macroscopic properties and experimental observables. Here, we introduce a streaming framework for MD simulations that provides direct access to all data generated during a running simulation. Instead of writing high-frequency output to disk, the framework enables user-defined analysis and processing routines to access simulation data in real time. To achieve this, we extend the Interactive Molecular Dynamics (IMD) protocol and implement an enhanced version, termed IMDv3, in the MD packages GROMACS, NAMD, and LAMMPS. We further introduce the Python package imdclient, which receives IMDv3 data streams and exposes them to external applications. To maximize usability, we add an imdclient-based reader to the MDAnalysis package, enabling streamed simulation data to be analyzed alongside conventional trajectory files. Benchmark results show that streaming can improve performance compared to simulations with high-frequency trajectory output. Example applications include live monitoring of custom variables, evaluation of velocity time-correlation functions with fast fluctuations, and real-time analysis of membrane pore currents.
tldr: This paper presents a streaming framework for molecular dynamics simulations that enables real-time access to all simulation data, bypassing storage limitations.
motivation: Current MD simulations generate petabytes of data but only store a fraction due to storage constraints, discarding information on fast processes. The authors aim to provide a method to access and analyze all data in real time.
method: The authors extend the Interactive Molecular Dynamics (IMD) protocol to IMDv3, implemented in GROMACS, NAMD, and LAMMPS, and develop the Python package imdclient to receive and expose data streams, with integration into MDAnalysis.
result: Benchmark results show that streaming can outperform simulations with high-frequency trajectory output. Example applications include live monitoring, velocity time-correlation functions, and real-time analysis of membrane pore currents.
conclusion: The framework enables analysis of fast processes previously discarded, potentially improving understanding of molecular dynamics and experimental observables.

title: Wide-field Mid-infrared Cavity-enhanced Upconversion Imaging
authors: Yue Song, Jianan Fang, Wen Zhang, Yijing Li, Ben Sun, Zhiwei Jia, Kun Huang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) spectral imaging enables precise target identification and analysis by capturing rich chemical fingerprints, which calls for high-sensitivity broadband MIR imagers at room temperature. Here, we devise and implement a continuous-wave pumping MIR upconversion imaging system based on external-cavity enhancement, which favors a large field of view, a low cavity loss, and a high spectral resolution. The involved optical cavity is constructed in an integrated fashion by utilizing one crystal facet as a cavity mirror, which allows a 43-fold power enhancement for the single-longitudinal-mode pump at 1064 nm. In combination with the chirped-poled crystal design, high-fidelity and wide-field spectral imaging mapping is permitted to facilitate an acceptance angle up to 28.5[MATH] over a spectral coverage of 2.5--5 [MATH]m. Moreover, a thermal locking approach is used to stabilize the cavity at the high-power operation, eliminating active feedback and ensuring long-term stability. A proof-of-principle demonstration is presented to showcase real-time observation of CO[MATH] gas injection dynamics. The implemented MIR upconversion imager features wide-field operation, high detection sensitivity, and compact footprint, which would benefit subsequent applications including environment monitoring, gas leakage inspection, and medical diagnostics.
tldr: This paper presents a mid-infrared upconversion imaging system using cavity-enhanced continuous-wave pumping for wide-field, high-sensitivity spectral imaging.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity broadband mid-infrared imaging at room temperature for applications like environmental monitoring and medical diagnostics.
method: An external-cavity enhancement design with a chirped-poled crystal and thermal locking for stability, achieving 43-fold pump power enhancement.
result: Demonstrated wide-field imaging with acceptance angle up to 28.5° over 2.5–5 μm spectral range, and real-time CO2 gas injection observation.
conclusion: The compact, high-sensitivity imager benefits applications in gas leakage inspection and medical diagnostics, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Semiclassical Propagation And The Dynamics Of Configuration Space
authors: V. S. Morales-Salgado
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work explores the non-relativistic quantum propagator [MATH] as a solution of the Schr\"odinger equation. We suppose that the propagator takes the form [MATH], generalizing the usual WKB ansatz by allowing an additive exponent [MATH] whose role as a measure of quantumness is investigated. Since [MATH] is subject to the assumption that it is a solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, here we are further interested in the role of [MATH] and its interpretation as a measure of quantumness. Several systems are studied as concrete examples to illustrate this approach. Furthermore, a proposal to generalize it for fields is put forward. This is tested for some simple systems. Finally, the possibilities to use this approach for the case of systems whose dynamics are controlled by the Hamiltonian constraint are analyzed.
tldr: This paper generalizes the WKB ansatz for the quantum propagator by introducing an additive exponent as a measure of quantumness, but does not connect to the user's research interests.
motivation: To explore a semiclassical propagation method and quantify quantumness in configuration space dynamics.
method: The propagator is assumed to take a generalized WKB form with an additive exponent, and the Hamilton-Jacobi equation is used to derive conditions; examples are studied.
result: The additive exponent serves as a measure of quantumness; the approach is tested on several systems and extended to fields.
conclusion: The method may be applicable to systems with Hamiltonian constraints, but no direct implications for information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems are discussed.

title: The Peculiar Response Of Kelvin-Voigt Chains With A Free End
authors: Matthias Kr\"uger Rupayan Saha
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exactly solve a model of a heterogeneous chain of overdamped, harmonically coupled particles with momentum-conserving dissipation. Despite being governed by a non-symmetric drift operator, the system admits an analytical diagonalization by use of a forward-difference transformation. In case of one free end, the response matrix shows a peculiar staircase form: the response of particle i to a force acting on particle j is independent of the properties and the length of the chain-part between i and j. For rank-deficient interaction matrices, the state space is decomposed into free and constrained subspaces. We demonstrate that this separation has clear physical consequences: the free subspace governs steady state responses, while the constraint subspace governs the relaxation after cessation of forcing. These results establish a framework for analyzing heterogeneous overdamped dynamics with momentum conservation.
tldr: This paper solves a model of overdamped harmonic chains with momentum-conserving dissipation, revealing a staircase response matrix and decomposition into free and constrained subspaces.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of heterogeneous overdamped chains with momentum conservation, which is a fundamental problem in statistical physics.
method: Exact analytical diagonalization using a forward-difference transformation for a non-symmetric drift operator.
result: The response matrix exhibits a staircase form where the response between particles is independent of intermediate chain properties; state space splits into free and constrained subspaces governing steady-state and relaxation dynamics.
conclusion: Provides a framework for analyzing heterogeneous overdamped dynamics with momentum conservation, with potential applications in soft matter or biological systems.

title: Variational Contraction Conditions For Iterative Algorithms In Multi-Population Discrete-Time Regularized Mean-Field Games
authors: Tamer Ba\c{s}ar U\u{g}ur Ayd{\i}n
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the contraction conditions of iterative algorithms for stationary and finite-horizon discrete-time regularized mean-field games (MFGs) with multiple populations, where each population only interacts with the state distributions of the other populations. Due to the high dimensionality caused by the interaction of different populations, contraction rates for these algorithms cannot, in general, be expressed in terms of radicals. By studying the dynamics of these iterative algorithms and assuming that the system components of each population's MFG are Lipschitz continuous, we present explicit (eventual) contraction conditions for each algorithm in any normed space, relying only on these Lipschitz parameters. As a consequence of these contraction conditions, we provide convergence rates of finite-horizon mean-field equilibria to infinite-horizon stationary (and non-stationary) mean-field equilibria (MFEs), under restrictions on a variational characterization of the dynamics of these iterative algorithms. In the single-population case, the restrictions we impose on this variational characterization to obtain these convergence results are less restrictive than previous results in the literature.
tldr: This paper studies contraction conditions for iterative algorithms in multi-population discrete-time regularized mean-field games, focusing on convergence rates and equilibria.
motivation: To address the high dimensionality and interaction complexity in multi-population mean-field games, and to provide explicit contraction conditions for iterative algorithms.
method: The authors analyze dynamics of iterative algorithms assuming Lipschitz continuous system components, and derive contraction conditions in any normed space using variational characterizations.
result: Explicit contraction conditions are presented for each algorithm, and convergence rates of finite-horizon equilibria to infinite-horizon equilibria are provided under certain restrictions.
conclusion: The results extend previous single-population results to multi-population settings with less restrictive conditions, but the work is purely mathematical and not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Irremediably Singular Quantum Branched Covers
authors: Alexandru Chirvasitu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Natsume-Olsen non-commutative spheres [MATH] dualize for rational deformation parameters to provide examples of quantum branched covers over their respective centers' maximal spectra, embeddable into locally trivial [MATH] bundles precisely when said spheres are classical; this, despite the bundles in question being of finite type over dimensional strata. The proof of the noted rigidity phenomenon relies on the quantum analogue of the 3-sphere's Heegaard splitting as a pushout of two solid tori.
tldr: This paper studies non-commutative spheres and quantum branched covers, focusing on rigidity phenomena when deformation parameters are rational.
motivation: To understand the structure of Natsume-Olsen non-commutative spheres and their dual quantum branched covers, particularly when they can be embedded into locally trivial bundles.
method: Uses quantum analogues of classical topology, such as Heegaard splitting of the 3-sphere, and algebraic geometry techniques for non-commutative spaces.

conclusion: The work highlights deep constraints in non-commutative geometry, but its direct relevance to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is minimal.

title: Topological Analysis In $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$anisotropic Sector And Nuclear Space On $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$quantum Deformed Algebra
authors: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this article is to develop and analyze [MATH]topological analysis of the classical nuclear space within the general framework of [MATH]calculus. We begin by introducing the [MATH]Gamma functions, establishing their main properties and their connection with the deformed factorials. We develop a rigorous analytic and functional-analytic framework for holomorphic functions governed by a general [MATH]deformation, where [MATH] is a meromorphic kernel satisfying [MATH]. A Stirling-type asymptotic expansion is established for the [MATH]deformed Gamma function [MATH], yielding precise exponential quadratic growth estimates driven by the asymptotics of the deformed factorial [MATH]. These asymptotics induce sharp coefficient bounds and Cauchy-type inequalities for [MATH]entire functions. Based on these estimates, we introduce [MATH]weighted Banach and Fr\'echet spaces of holomorphic functions, together with deformation dependent pseudo-norms and valuation maps. Within this setting, we define [MATH]discs and anisotropic sectors adapted to the deformation geometry and prove [MATH]analogues of the Cauchy-Hadamard theorem, the Borel-Carath\'eodory inequality and Phragm\'en-Lindel\"of type growth principles. title: Learning Dynamical Systems With Biochemically Informed Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Luis L. Fonseca, Reinhard C. Laubenbacher, Lucas B\"ottcher
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordinary differential equation models of biochemical reactions are often formulated as stoichiometric systems in which the dynamics arise from a collection of interacting processes. A central challenge is that the functional form of each process is rarely known a priori and may be difficult to infer from data. We propose biochemically informed neural ordinary differential equations (BINODEs), a neural-ODE framework that retains the stoichiometric structure of mechanistic models while representing individual processes by neural networks. In BINODEs, the outputs of neural network processes (NNPs) are mapped to state derivatives through a linear layer analogous to a stoichiometric matrix. This architecture allows biological side information, such as process-specific inputs, sign constraints, and monotonicity assumptions, to be built directly into the model. We characterize the approximation properties of NNPs for several standard biochemical rate laws and show that the proposed framework recovers both trajectories and process-level structure in Monod, Lotka--Volterra, pharmacokinetic, and ultradian endocrine models. These results suggest that BINODEs offer a useful compromise between mechanistic interpretability and data-driven flexibility for modeling partially known biochemical or biological dynamical systems.
tldr: BINODEs combine neural networks with stoichiometric ODE models to learn biochemical dynamics from data while preserving interpretability.
motivation: Traditional mechanistic models require known functional forms for each process, which are often unknown; purely data-driven models lack interpretability.
method: A neural-ODE framework where each process is represented by a neural network, and state derivatives are computed via a linear layer analogous to a stoichiometric matrix, allowing incorporation of biological side information.
result: The framework accurately recovers trajectories and process-level structure in several benchmark models (Monod, Lotka-Volterra, pharmacokinetic, ultradian endocrine).
conclusion: BINODEs offer a useful compromise between mechanistic interpretability and data-driven flexibility for modeling partially known biochemical systems.

title: Threshold-Safe Shock Absorption In A Compartmental Voter-Flow Model:\ A Conservative Impulse-Control Benchmark
authors: Alexander Omelchenko
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a deterministic threshold-safety problem for a reduced compartmental voter-flow model. An exogenous load enters an alienation reservoir; between releases the reservoir recovers exponentially. Near the mainstream baseline the compartmental dynamics have a linear-stability threshold \(\Delta_c\): below this level the mobilised component contracts, while above it transient amplification is possible. The paper introduces an impulse-control layer for this threshold mechanism. The threshold is obtained from the local stability boundary of the reduced dynamical system, the exposure functional is tied to positive logarithmic amplification, and the scalar reservoir model is proved to be a conservative envelope of the nonlinear voter-flow dynamics. This bridge yields explicit safety benchmarks: the single-release exposure and its zero buffer, the complete-relaxation splitting problem with fixed per-release overhead, the finite-recovery constant-peak profile, and the fixed-horizon capacity frontier \(\Delta_c(1+\rho T)\). The scalar recurrence used after the reduction is the familiar leaky-reservoir skeleton also found in multiple-dose pharmacokinetics, fractionated radiotherapy, reservoir operation, and setup-cost scheduling. Its role here is to make the threshold regimes of the compartmental shock-absorption model analytically transparent.
tldr: This paper develops a deterministic threshold-safety problem for a compartmental voter-flow model using impulse control, with applications to shock absorption.
motivation: To provide analytical benchmarks for threshold safety in a reduced voter-flow model, motivated by analogies to pharmacokinetics and reservoir operation.
method: The authors formulate a reduced compartmental model with an alienation reservoir, derive a linear-stability threshold, and introduce an impulse-control layer to manage exogenous loads.
result: Explicit safety benchmarks are derived, including single-release exposure, zero buffer, complete-relaxation splitting, finite-recovery constant-peak profile, and fixed-horizon capacity frontier.
conclusion: The scalar recurrence provides a transparent analytical framework for threshold regimes in compartmental shock-absorption models, with potential extensions to other fields.

title: Accuracy Analysis Of The Proxy Point Method With Applications To Some Toeplitz Matrices
authors: Jianlin Xia Mikhail Lepilov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For some kernel matrices, low-rank approximations can be quickly obtained via analytic techniques. One important class of analytic methods that has received attention in recent years is based on the use of proxy points. Accuracy analysis for various proxy point methods has often been heuristic in nature, other than for certain special kernels. For more general cases, the methods lack an explicit number or location of proxy points required to yield a particular approximation accuracy. In this work, we carry out new analysis of a proxy point method that is applicable to general complex-analytic kernels. An intuitive way of choosing proxy points is used to show explicit error bounds. Such bounds decay exponentially with regard to the number of proxy points. This also leads to convenient estimates of numerical ranks of relevant kernel matrices. To showcase the utility of this new analysis, we apply it to design a new sublinear-time hierarchically semiseparable approximation method for certain Toeplitz matrices, including ones that frequently arise from real-world applications. This allows, for example, inversion of such matrices with lower computational complexity compared with existing direct methods. Some extensions of these ideas are also discussed.
tldr: This paper presents a rigorous error analysis of proxy point methods for low-rank approximations of kernel matrices, with applications to Toeplitz matrices, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Proxy point methods for low-rank approximations lacked rigorous error bounds for general complex-analytic kernels, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors derive explicit exponential error bounds for a proxy point method using an intuitive choice of proxy points, and apply it to design a sublinear-time hierarchically semiseparable approximation for Toeplitz matrices.
result: Error bounds decay exponentially with the number of proxy points, enabling estimates of numerical ranks and efficient inversion of Toeplitz matrices.
conclusion: The analysis provides a theoretical foundation for proxy point methods and yields practical algorithms for structured matrices, with potential extensions to other kernels.

title: An Exact Continuous Conductance Formulation Of The Hamiltonian Path Problem
authors: A. Sadovsky
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hamiltonian Path Problem is formulated as a continuous minimization problem on conductances assigned to an Ohmic network associated with the given graph. The objective function is a sum of two penalty terms that collectively enforce a set of conditions sufficient for a subgraph of the original graph to be a Hamiltonian path. The objective function is nonconvex. The main result (Theorem 1) shows that, provided the graph has a Hamiltonian path from [MATH] to [MATH], a conductance configuration is a global minimizer of the objective if and only if it corresponds to a Hamiltonian path.
tldr: This paper reformulates the Hamiltonian Path Problem as a continuous optimization over conductances in an Ohmic network, proving equivalence between global minimizers and Hamiltonian paths.
motivation: To provide an exact continuous formulation of the Hamiltonian Path Problem, potentially enabling new optimization approaches.
method: The problem is cast as minimizing a sum of two penalty terms over conductances assigned to edges of an Ohmic network, with conditions enforcing a Hamiltonian path.
result: Theorem 1 shows that if a Hamiltonian path exists, a conductance configuration is a global minimizer iff it corresponds to a Hamiltonian path.
conclusion: The work offers a novel continuous perspective on a classic combinatorial problem, but its practical implications and connections to physics are not explored.

title: Spectral Analysis And Sine Transform Based Preconditioning For A Structure Preserving Stabilized Scheme Approximating The Space-fractional Allen Cahn Equation With Logarithmic Potential
authors: Danyal Ahmad, Stefano Serra-Capizzano, Muhammad Sohaib, Cristina Tablino-Possio
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an initial boundary value problem of the space fractional Allen-Cahn equation with logarithmic Flory-Huggins potential. As an approximation technique, first-order weighted and shifted Grunwald difference formulae of the left and right fractional derivatives are used. The main focus of the present work is to study the spectral features of the underlying matrices and matrix sequences and to design proper preconditioners based on the spectral information. Then a computational and spectral analysis of the resulting preconditioned matrix sequences is performed. Numerical evidence and a short list of open problems complete the current study.
tldr: This paper develops preconditioners for solving the space-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with logarithmic potential, focusing on spectral analysis and numerical linear algebra.

method: Uses weighted and shifted Grünwald difference formulas to discretize fractional derivatives, analyzes the spectral properties of the resulting Toeplitz-like matrices, and proposes sine-transform-based preconditioners.
result: The preconditioned matrix sequences show clustered spectra, leading to fast convergence of iterative methods; numerical experiments confirm efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioners are effective for this class of problems, with open problems including extension to higher dimensions and time-dependent potentials.

title: SinFormer: A Tailored Transformer For Robust Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification
authors: Liu Yang, Qiang Li, Xiaoyang Ren
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of wireless and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, ensuring secure and reliable device identification has become a significant challenge. Traditional security techniques, such as IP or MAC address-based authentication, are susceptible to spoofing, whereas Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification (RFFI) offers a more secure alternative by exploiting the unique hardware imperfections in devices' RF signals. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based framework for RFFI that enhances both accuracy and reliability in challenging RF environments. The core of our approach is the Signal Inception Transformer (SinFormer), which leverages a specialized multi-scale self-attention mechanism to effectively capture both large-scale and fine-grained fingerprints in signals, significantly improving identification accuracy. To further enhance robustness and reliability, we introduce a two-stage training strategy that enables the model to learn general signal features and maintain performance under adverse conditions, such as low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) or channel variations. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a real-world dataset. Experimental results show that the SinFormer framework consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy and robustness across diverse and challenging scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes a Transformer-based deep learning framework for radio frequency fingerprint identification to improve device authentication security.
motivation: Traditional device authentication methods like IP/MAC are vulnerable to spoofing, and RFFI offers a more secure alternative by exploiting hardware imperfections in RF signals.
method: The authors introduce SinFormer, a Signal Inception Transformer with a multi-scale self-attention mechanism, and a two-stage training strategy to enhance robustness under low SNR and channel variations.
result: Experimental results on a real-world dataset show that SinFormer outperforms existing methods in accuracy and robustness across diverse scenarios.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a reliable solution for device identification in challenging RF environments, with potential applications in IoT security.

title: Geometry-Preserving Nudged Elastic Band And Dimer Methods Under Anisotropic Force Uncertainty
authors: Yangshuai Wang Yifan Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nudged elastic band (NEB) and Dimer methods are standard tools for computing minimum-energy paths and index-one saddle points in atomistic transition problems. They are increasingly driven by surrogate or learned force models, whose force errors are often anisotropic and spatially varying near transition states and defect cores, where saddle-search iterations are most sensitive. We introduce uncertainty-aware NEB and Dimer methods (UA-NEB, UA-Dimer) that use covariance as an optimizer-level reliability metric while preserving the mean-potential saddle-search equations: an oblique normal projection for NEB and covariance-weighted rotation and translation for Dimer. Both algorithms fit Robbins--Monro recursions; under a local Lyapunov stability hypothesis, verified explicitly for a canonical UA-NEB setting and stated as a hypothesis for UA-Dimer, the stochastic iterations converge almost surely within the corresponding local stability neighborhood. In the analytic benchmark, UA-NEB reduces mean barrier error by [MATH] relative to stochastic NEB and UA-Dimer reduces the reflected-gradient residual by [MATH]; in the 127-atom tungsten-vacancy benchmark, full UA-NEB reduces mean barrier error by [MATH] relative to stochastic NEB and by [MATH] relative to diagonal covariance weighting. These results show that anisotropic uncertainty is most useful when embedded in the constrained geometry of the optimizer rather than collapsed into a scalar acquisition or trust criterion.

motivation: Surrogate force models in atomistic simulations have anisotropic errors near transition states, degrading saddle-search accuracy.
method: The authors incorporate covariance information into NEB and Dimer algorithms via oblique normal projection and covariance-weighted rotation/translation, formulating them as Robbins-Monro recursions.
result: UA-NEB and UA-Dimer reduce mean barrier error and reflected-gradient residual significantly in benchmarks compared to stochastic or diagonal-covariance methods.
conclusion: Anisotropic uncertainty is best exploited within the optimizer's constrained geometry, not collapsed into scalar criteria.

title: Orbit Decomposition Statistics For Discrete Dynamical Systems: The Ces\`aro Mean And A Large Deviation Principle
authors: Sun Woo Park Gunther Cornelissen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If a self-map [MATH] has a dynamical zeta function with nonzero radius of convergence [MATH] and the Ces\`aro mean [MATH] of [MATH] exists and is positive, we show a large deviation principle for the number of prime orbits occurring in the decomposition of a general orbit of length [MATH] (an element of the free abelian monoid generated by the prime orbits or, equivalently, a prime orbit of a finite multiset in [MATH]) with speed [MATH] and universal rate function equal to that of the Poisson distribution with unit mean. We also show a large deviation principle for more general strongly additive functions. The theory applies, for example, to endomorphisms of algebraic groups over finite fields, additive cellular automata, and automorphisms of some solenoids.

method: Analytic number theory techniques, including dynamical zeta functions and asymptotic analysis of orbit counts.

title: Incremental Svd For Large-Scale Dynamic Matrices: Accuracy, Subspace Stability, Refresh Strategies, And Financial Factor-Based Risk Models
authors: Stilyan Staykov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Return panels, covariances, and large feature matrices evolve one observation or one entry at a time, yet downstream models require an up-to-date low-rank factorization [MATH] on every tick -- a regime where full SVD is prohibitive and existing alternatives sacrifice either singular vectors, singular values, or long-horizon stability. We present a practical, metric-driven study of Brand-style incremental SVD, built around a unified engine that handles row appends, column appends, rank-1 entry updates, and metrics tracking within a single framework, with two core contributions. For rank-1 entry updates, we derive an explicit projection-based rule [MATH] that keeps rank fixed while discarding only the out-of-subspace remainder in a quantifiable way, turning Brand's rank-suppression heuristic into an operational scheme. We then treat refresh scheduling as a first-class design axis, systematically comparing periodic, error-threshold, angle-threshold, and adaptive-rank policies on the accuracy-latency frontier. A unified framework tracks error ratios, principal angles, explained variance, and per-update runtime on long synthetic streams and a multi-asset ETF factor model for covariance and portfolio-risk estimation. With a sensible rank and refresh cadence, incremental SVD matches full-SVD accuracy within a few percent at a fraction of the cost, scaling to high-frequency regimes where batch SVDs are infeasible.
tldr: This paper presents an incremental SVD algorithm for large-scale dynamic matrices, focusing on accuracy, stability, and refresh strategies, with application to financial risk models.
motivation: Full SVD is computationally prohibitive for high-frequency updates in financial factor models, and existing incremental methods sacrifice accuracy or stability.
method: The authors develop a unified incremental SVD engine handling row/column appends and rank-1 updates, with explicit projection-based update rules and systematic comparison of refresh policies.
result: Incremental SVD matches full SVD accuracy within a few percent at a fraction of the cost, enabling real-time low-rank factorization for high-frequency data.
conclusion: The method scales to regimes where batch SVD is infeasible, with implications for financial risk modeling and other dynamic matrix applications.

title: Orthant-Monotonic Norms And Additive D-Stability
authors: Michael Margaliot Ron Ofir
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matrix measures induced by vector norms are widely used in contraction theory of nonlinear dynamical systems. A natural and important robustness question is whether negativity of a matrix measure is preserved under arbitrary nonnegative diagonal damping. Matrix measures with this property have been called admissible. We show that an induced matrix measure is admissible if and only if the underlying norm is orthant-monotonic. motivation: To understand which matrix measures (induced by vector norms) remain negative when arbitrary nonnegative diagonal damping is added, a robustness property called admissibility.
method: The authors prove that an induced matrix measure is admissible if and only if the underlying norm is orthant-monotonic, and show this class is maximal for uniform preservation of contraction.
result: Admissible matrix measures are exactly those induced by orthant-monotonic norms; this gives a geometric characterization and clarifies the role of orthant-monotonicity in additive D-stability and diffusion-induced instability.

title: Optimized Multilevel Monte Carlo Methods In Banach Spaces
