title: Smooth Integrability Of Diffeomorphisms
authors: Kazuyuki Yagasaki
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the notion of integrability introduced by Bogoyavlenskij for vector fields, we propose a definition of smooth integrability for general diffeomorphisms. In brief, we say that a diffeomorphism is integrable if it commutes with the flows of {commutative} vector fields and shares their first integrals. We establish a Liouville-Arnold type theorem and prove that on connected invariant level sets of the first integrals, a smoothly integrable diffeomorphism is conjugate to a skew translation on a toroidal cylinder, and in particular, when the level sets are compact, the induced dynamics is quasiperiodic, as in the classical Hamiltonian case. We further show that linear diffeomorphisms on real or complex Euclidean spaces are integrable in our sense, as is the case for linear vector fields in the sense of Bogoyavlenskij, and symplectic diffeomorphisms that are integrable in their standard Liouville-type definition are integrable in our framework. We also modify the cotangent lift construction, which is useful in the treatment of integrability of vector fields, for diffeomorphisms, and show that integrability is preserved under this correspondence. Several examples are provided to illustrate the scope of the theory.
tldr: This paper defines smooth integrability for diffeomorphisms and proves a Liouville-Arnold type theorem showing that integrable diffeomorphisms are conjugate to skew translations on toroidal cylinders.
motivation: To extend the concept of integrability from vector fields to diffeomorphisms, motivated by Bogoyavlenskij's work.
method: The authors propose a definition of smooth integrability for diffeomorphisms based on commuting flows and first integrals, then prove a conjugacy theorem and examine examples.
result: Smoothly integrable diffeomorphisms are conjugate to skew translations on toroidal cylinders; on compact level sets the dynamics is quasiperiodic. Linear diffeomorphisms and symplectic integrable diffeomorphisms are integrable in this sense.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for integrability of diffeomorphisms analogous to that for vector fields, with potential applications in dynamical systems.

title: A Perron-Frobenius Strong Threshold Theorem For (a, B, P, {\phi}) Balanced Bilinear Models, And The Role Of Left And Right Perron Eigenvectors In Mathematical Epidemiology
authors: Florin Avram, Rim Adenane, Andrei-Dan Halanay, Andras Horvath, Sei Zhen Khong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper started as a review of seven results pertaining to a family of bilinear models with rank one NGM introduced by Fall, Iggidr, Sallet and Bonzi, which utilize the explicit eigenvectors of the NGM to compute the unique endemic equilibrium (EE), and Lyapunov functions at both the disease free equilibrium (DFE) and EE, and of results of Shuai and Van den Driessche (2013), which essentially deal with the same "DFE -EE stability exchange" in the non-rank one case, when the eigenvectors are not explicit. Recently, these results were complemented by Earn and McCluskey (2025), who proved as well a ``strong threshold theorem", namely that when the DFE is unstable, a second equilibrium which is globally asymptotically stable must exist. Below, we obtain in Theorem some results that extend beyond rank one. For example, a nontrivial positive equilibrium exists if and only if the spectral equation \(\rho(\widetilde K(S))=1\), admits a strictly positive solution. Also, we showed that Bonzi-Iggidr-Sallet bilinear models with rank one NGM may be classified in two classes, with slight variations in the eigenvector formulas, and that extensions in the presence of feedback from infectious to susceptible are possible. Another takeout from the previous works, which we clarify in a revisit of the seven results in the rank one case, is that Lyapunov functions for both the DFE and the EE may be constructed using as weights the left Perron eigenvector [MATH] of the \NGM\ (NGM) [MATH], where [MATH] denote all the non-infectious variables, and when a positive ODE leaves a siphon face, it does so along the right Perron eigenvector [MATH] of [MATH]. The question of whether this continues to be true beyond rank one is explored in ongoing work.

motivation: To generalize known results about equilibrium stability in bilinear epidemiological models beyond rank-one cases and to clarify the role of left and right Perron eigenvectors.
method: Mathematical analysis of bilinear ODE models with rank-one NGM, using spectral theory and Lyapunov function construction with Perron eigenvectors.
result: A strong threshold theorem is proved: when the disease-free equilibrium is unstable, a globally asymptotically stable endemic equilibrium exists. The paper also classifies rank-one models and explores extensions with feedback.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for stability analysis in bilinear epidemiological models, with ongoing work to extend beyond rank-one NGMs.

title: Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport: Localization Bounds And Affine Case Analysis
authors: Long Nguyen-Chi, Nam Nguyen, Binh Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic regularization has emerged as a potential alternative to the popular entropic regularization in computational optimal transport, offering the theoretical advantage of producing sparse couplings through its hinge density structure. Despite recent progress in one-dimensional settings and general upper bounds, fundamental questions about the localization rate of QOT optimizers around the Monge coupling have remained open. In this work, we establish a general lower bound showing that the support of the QOT optimizer cannot concentrate around the Monge graph faster than order [MATH] in the directed Hausdorff distance, matching the conjectured optimal exponent under standard regularity assumptions in . We also show that the QOT value gap controls the mean-squared deviation [MATH] by the scale of [MATH]. title: Robust Ergodic Control Of Jump-Diffusion Systems Under Drift And Intensity Uncertainty
authors: Abel Azze, Bernardo D'auria, Giorgio Ferrari
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a regulation problem for stochastic systems subject to both continuous fluctuations and rare but significant shocks, modeled as a jump-diffusion with uncertainty in both the drift and the jump intensity. Such settings arise in applications including inventory control, cash management, and capacity planning. We formulate the problem as a robust ergodic singular control problem in which a decision maker applies upward and downward interventions while accounting for model ambiguity through entropy-penalized distortions. The resulting max-min problem involves a long-run average performance criterion. We show that the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation reduces to a nonlinear integro-differential free-boundary problem with a tractable structure. The worst-case model exhibits a bang-bang form, and the optimal policy is characterized by reflecting barriers. Under exponentially distributed jumps, the problem further reduces to a system of ordinary differential equations, enabling efficient numerical computation.
tldr: This paper studies robust ergodic control of jump-diffusion systems with drift and intensity uncertainty, focusing on applications like inventory and cash management.
motivation: To address regulation problems in stochastic systems with both continuous fluctuations and rare shocks, where model ambiguity exists in drift and jump intensity.
method: Formulates a robust ergodic singular control problem with entropy-penalized distortions, reducing the HJB equation to a nonlinear integro-differential free-boundary problem.
result: The worst-case model is bang-bang, and the optimal policy is characterized by reflecting barriers; under exponential jumps, the problem reduces to ODEs for efficient computation.
conclusion: Provides a tractable framework for robust control of jump-diffusions, with potential extensions to other applications.

title: Stochastic Maximum Principle For Optimal Control Of Infinitely Delayed Systems Of Functional Type In Infinite Dimensions
authors: Guanwei Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the optimal control problems of stochastic evolution equations with infinite delay of general functional type. By introducing a non-anticipative path derivative and its infinite-window dual operator, we derive the infinitely anticipated backward stochastic evolution equation (IABSEE) as the adjoint equation, and establish both necessary and sufficient maximum principles. As an application, we solve an infinite-delay linear-quadratic (LQ) control problem and obtain the explicit optimal control.
tldr: This paper develops a stochastic maximum principle for optimal control of infinite-dimensional systems with infinite delay, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend optimal control theory to stochastic evolution equations with infinite delay in infinite dimensions, which is a challenging mathematical problem.
method: Introduces a non-anticipative path derivative and its infinite-window dual operator to derive an infinitely anticipated backward stochastic evolution equation (IABSEE) as the adjoint equation, then establishes necessary and sufficient maximum principles.
result: Obtains both necessary and sufficient maximum principles for optimal control of such systems, and solves an infinite-delay linear-quadratic control problem explicitly.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for optimal control of infinite-delay stochastic systems, with potential applications in economics, biology, or engineering, but not in quantum physics.

title: Wino: A Weak-Form Physics Informed Neural Operator For Hyperelasticity On Variable Domains
authors: Bokai Zhu, Qinghui Zhang, Timon Rabczuk
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a Weak-form Physics-Informed Neural Operator (WINO), a data-free framework that combines the efficiency of neural operators with the geometric flexibility of the [MATH]-finite element method ([MATH]-FEM). [MATH]-FEM is an unfitted method that accommodates geometric variations without body-fitted meshes, where the domain geometry is represented by the level-set function [MATH]. To impose the boundary conditions, Dirichlet problems adopt the [MATH]-FEM lifting so only the homogeneous displacement contribution is learned, whereas traction-driven Neumann problems additionally predict the auxiliary fields necessary for the unfitted weak formulation. Parameters are trained by minimizing squared weak-form residuals aligned with [MATH]-FEM together with squared penalties on the cut-cell auxiliary equations, which removes the need for large paired datasets of converged reference solutions. After training, WINO outputs can seed the nonlinear [MATH]-FEM solvers as neural operator warm starts (NOWS), which reduce iteration counts relative to traditional cold-started solvers. Numerical benchmarks show that WINO achieves high accuracy below 0.04 across all benchmarks, while reducing total computational time by 50--80\% compared with purely data-driven methods.
tldr: WINO is a data-free neural operator for hyperelasticity on variable domains using weak-form physics-informed learning and unfitted FEM.
motivation: To develop a fast and accurate solver for hyperelasticity problems on complex geometries without requiring large datasets or body-fitted meshes.
method: Combines a neural operator with the φ-FEM unfitted method, minimizing weak-form residuals and auxiliary equation penalties; trained without data, outputs can warm-start nonlinear solvers.
result: Achieves high accuracy (error < 0.04) and reduces total computational time by 50–80% compared to data-driven methods.
conclusion: WINO provides an efficient, geometry-flexible framework for hyperelasticity, with potential for broader applications in computational mechanics.

title: Finding Koopman Invariant Subspaces Via Personalized PageRank
authors: Hyukpyo Hong, Qin Li, Matthew J. Colbrook, Hanbaek Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting a finite dictionary of observables whose span is Koopman-invariant is a central challenge in data-driven Koopman operator approximation. We address this problem by exploiting zero-block structure in Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) matrices. We show that any sub-dictionary whose span is Koopman-invariant induces an exact zero block in the EDMD matrix, even for finite data. We then show that such blocks can be detected by applying PageRank to a row-normalized EDMD matrix constructed from a large initial dictionary. The theory extends to approximately invariant subspaces and yields stronger guarantees for personalized PageRank (PPR) when the seed observables lie inside the target block and reach all observables in that block. Combining EDMD concentration bounds with PageRank perturbation theory gives end-to-end detection guarantees with [MATH] finite-sample scaling and explicit constants. More generally, without assuming an invariant subspace exists, high PPR mass on a sub-dictionary controls discounted multi-step leakage from the seed observables. Numerical experiments on the Duffing oscillator, Van der Pol oscillator, Lorenz system, and a three-well Ramachandran potential suggest that the method identifies compact, interpretable dictionaries with accurate predictions.
tldr: This paper uses personalized PageRank to identify Koopman invariant subspaces from EDMD matrices, with applications in dynamical systems.
motivation: Selecting a finite dictionary of observables that spans a Koopman-invariant subspace is a key challenge in data-driven Koopman operator approximation.
method: The authors show that invariant subspaces induce zero blocks in EDMD matrices and detect these blocks using personalized PageRank on a row-normalized EDMD matrix.
result: The method provides finite-sample guarantees and identifies compact, interpretable dictionaries, demonstrated on several nonlinear oscillators and a potential energy surface.
conclusion: The approach offers a principled way to discover Koopman-invariant subspaces, with potential for improved prediction and interpretability in dynamical systems.

title: Sharp Convergence Rates And Optimal Weights For Cimmino's Reflection Algorithm

title: Age Of Information Optimization For Status Updates In Integrated Sensing And Communication Systems
authors: Marco Zanni, Mohamad Assaad, Touraj Soleymani
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study age of information (AoI) optimization for status updating in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. We consider a discrete-time architecture in which a base station interacts with a physical environment and a remote monitor, and at each time slot can operate in one of three modes: sensing, communication, or joint sensing and communication. Each mode is unreliable and incurs a different operational cost. The objective is to minimize a discounted infinite-horizon cost that combines the AoI at the monitor with action-dependent sensing and communication costs. For the single source scenario, we formulate the problem as a Markov decision process with a two-dimensional AoI state and prove that the optimal stationary policy admits an ordered threshold structure in the AoI state space. Since the AoI evolves over an infinite space, we truncate the state space to reduce complexity and rigorously bound the resulting error. The analysis analytically determines the truncation size needed to keep the error below a given threshold. For the multi-source scenario, we formulate the scheduling problem as a restless multi-armed bandit. We develop both a Whittle index policy and an approximate Whittle index policy for scheduling under two different regimes, one where indexability is guaranteed, and one where it is not. Numerical results illustrate the structure of the optimal policy in the single-source case and show that the proposed approximate Whittle index policy performs comparably to the Whittle index policy in the indexable regime, while remaining effective beyond it.
tldr: This paper optimizes age of information in integrated sensing and communication systems using MDP and restless multi-armed bandit approaches.
motivation: To minimize the cost combining AoI and operational costs in ISAC systems with unreliable modes.
method: Formulates single-source problem as MDP with threshold policy; multi-source as restless bandit with Whittle index policies.
result: Optimal policy has ordered threshold structure; approximate Whittle index policy performs comparably to exact one.
conclusion: Provides analytical truncation bounds and effective scheduling policies for AoI optimization in ISAC.

title: Consistent Identification Of Top-$K$ Nodes In Noisy Networks
authors: Eric D. Kolaczyk Hui Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying the most influential nodes in a network, typically using centrality measures, is a central task in applied network analysis. However, real-world networks are often constructed from noisy or incomplete data, which can distort rankings and lead to errors in identifying the true top-[MATH] nodes. In this paper, we study how network noise affects the recovery of the true top-[MATH] node set based on degree centrality. Specifically, we consider a noisy network observation in which edges are randomly added or removed according to a probabilistic noise model, and analyze the resulting empirical top-[MATH] set. We show that top-[MATH] recovery under network noise is governed by the relationship between the degree gap and the noise magnitude, which separates recoverable and unrecoverable regimes. To quantify ranking stability, we derive upper and lower bounds on the expected discrepancy between the empirical and true top-[MATH] sets in a general framework and for specific network models. We also extend the analysis to eigenvector centrality, showing that similar noise-gap tradeoffs arise in spectral rankings. Simulation studies support our theoretical findings and illustrate the practical impact of network noise across a range of settings.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of network noise on the identification of top-K nodes by degree and eigenvector centrality, establishing noise-gap tradeoffs for recovery.
motivation: Real-world networks are often noisy, which can distort centrality rankings and lead to errors in identifying influential nodes. The authors aim to understand when and how the true top-K set can be reliably recovered under edge noise.
method: The authors model network noise as random edge additions and deletions, analyze the expected discrepancy between empirical and true top-K sets, and derive upper and lower bounds for degree centrality. They extend the analysis to eigenvector centrality using spectral perturbation theory.
result: Top-K recovery is governed by the relationship between the degree gap and noise magnitude, with a sharp transition between recoverable and unrecoverable regimes. Similar noise-gap tradeoffs hold for eigenvector centrality.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical guarantees for ranking stability in noisy networks and highlight practical limitations. Future work may extend to other centrality measures and more complex noise models.

title: On The Sample Complexity Of Robust Binary Hypothesis Testing
authors: Shankar Vallinayagam, Ankit Pensia, Varun Jog

title: Efficient Numerical Schemes For A Two-Phase Hydrodynamical Model Of Active Liquid Crystals And Solids
authors: Xuelong Gu, Guanghua Ji, Qi Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose several linear, fully decoupled numerical schemes with first- and second-order temporal accuracy for a novel Q-tensor-based two-phase hydrodynamic model describing the coupling of active nematic liquid crystal solutions with isotropic solid substrates. The model is derived from the generalized Onsager principle and includes nontrivial terms that contribute zero to the total free-energy dissipation. We prove that the proposed decoupled linear schemes are thermodynamically consistent at the discrete level. In the passive limit, the SGE-BDF1 and SGE-PDG schemes are unconditionally energy stable, while the SGE-BDF2 scheme is energy stable with respect to a modified energy under a standard boundedness assumption and a sufficiently large stabilization parameter. We perform extensive numerical simulations to investigate how activity and other model parameters affect active nematic fluid-solid interactions. Finally, we analyze the physical mechanisms underlying the observed behaviors, providing deeper insight into the dynamics of soft confined active nematic fluids.
tldr: This paper develops numerical schemes for a two-phase hydrodynamic model of active liquid crystals and solids, focusing on thermodynamic consistency and energy stability.
motivation: To efficiently simulate active nematic liquid crystal interactions with solid substrates, which is important for understanding soft confined active fluids.
method: Proposes linear, fully decoupled numerical schemes (SGE-BDF1, SGE-PDG, SGE-BDF2) based on the generalized Onsager principle, with proofs of thermodynamic consistency and energy stability.
result: The schemes are thermodynamically consistent at the discrete level; in the passive limit, SGE-BDF1 and SGE-PDG are unconditionally energy stable, while SGE-BDF2 is stable under certain conditions. Numerical simulations reveal how activity and parameters affect fluid-solid interactions.
conclusion: The work provides efficient numerical tools for studying active nematic fluids, but the physical insights are limited to the specific model and may not directly apply to quantum systems.

title: On The Geometry Of Sharp Minima
authors: Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give characterizations of sharp minimizers that emphasize their geometric properties. These include tilt invariance and weak upper gradient conditions. We relate sharp minimality to cusps in nonsmooth manifolds when interpreted locally as graphs and connect the rolling of tangent planes to the tilting of functions.

motivation: To better understand the geometric properties of sharp minimizers, which are important in optimization and nonsmooth analysis.
method: The authors use mathematical analysis to characterize sharp minimizers through tilt invariance and weak upper gradient conditions, and relate them to cusps in nonsmooth manifolds.
result: Sharp minimality is linked to cusps in nonsmooth manifolds and the rolling of tangent planes to function tilting.
conclusion: The findings offer new geometric insights into sharp minimizers, potentially impacting optimization theory and nonsmooth analysis.

title: Subgradient Methods On Manifolds With Lower Bounded Curvature
authors: G. C. Bento, J. X. Cruz Neto, J. O. Lopes, I. D. L. Melo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The subgradient method is a classical and foundational approach in non-smooth convex optimization; its simplicity, robustness, and role as a conceptual and algorithmic starting point have made it the backbone of many significant optimization algorithms. Motivated by classical Euclidean results and recent advances in first-order Riemannian optimization, we study the convergence of the subgradient method on Hadamard manifolds with lower bounded curvature. Assuming a nonempty solution set and employing a corresponding non-summable diminishing step-size condition, we establish convergence of the generated sequence [MATH] to a minimizer whenever at least one of the following holds: (a) the sequence [MATH] is bounded; (b) the solution set [MATH] is bounded; or (c) the step-sizes are square-summable ([MATH]). Additionally, we prove that if [MATH], the method achieves finite termination. motivation: To generalize classical subgradient methods from Euclidean spaces to curved manifolds, addressing non-smooth convex optimization in Riemannian settings.
method: The authors analyze the subgradient method on Hadamard manifolds with lower bounded curvature, using non-summable diminishing step-sizes and establishing convergence under boundedness or square-summability conditions.

title: Random-Subspace Frank--Wolfe Over Strongly Convex Sets
authors: Pierre-Louis Poirion, Sebastian Pokutta, Akiko Takeda
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frank--Wolfe methods avoid projections, but over curved feasible regions the full-space linear minimization oracle (LMO) can itself become the computational bottleneck. We introduce random-subspace Frank--Wolfe (RSFW), the first Frank--Wolfe framework, to our knowledge, that replaces the ambient LMO by exact LMOs over random low-dimensional affine sections of a general feasible set, while preserving feasibility in the original space. For smooth convex objectives over compact strongly convex feasible sets, we prove a dimension-explicit approximate-oracle inequality and derive the standard \(O(1/k)\) open-loop rate, with high-probability and almost-sure counterparts. Under short steps and a gradient lower bound, the same geometric control yields linear convergence, and we extend the sublinear theory to finite-sum stochastic gradients. We also show that random sections can improve the local curvature model controlling short steps: for smooth objectives, the quadratic model along a sampled section is governed by the compressed Hessian, yielding computable \(d\times d\) curvature constants for quadratic objectives over balls and ellipsoids. These results provide a geometric theory of oracle-side randomization in projection-free optimization.
tldr: This paper introduces a random-subspace Frank-Wolfe algorithm for optimization over strongly convex sets, with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Frank-Wolfe methods avoid projections but can be bottlenecked by the linear minimization oracle over curved feasible sets. The authors aim to reduce this cost by using random low-dimensional sections.
method: They propose RSFW, which replaces the full-space linear minimization oracle with exact LMOs over random low-dimensional affine sections of the feasible set, while maintaining feasibility. They analyze convergence for smooth convex objectives over strongly convex sets.
result: They prove an O(1/k) open-loop rate with high probability, linear convergence under short steps and gradient lower bound, and extend to stochastic gradients. They also show that random sections improve local curvature models.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric theory for oracle-side randomization in projection-free optimization, potentially improving efficiency for problems with expensive LMOs.

title: A Hybrid Discontinuous Galerkin Method With Isogeometric-Planewaves Coupling For Periodic Full-Potential Electronic Structure Calculations
authors: Baowei Lai, Xucheng Meng, Xiaoxu Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-potential electronic structure calculations for periodic systems retain the Coulomb singularity at the nuclei, which induces cusp behavior of the orbitals near the nuclei while leaving the interstitial region smooth. This multiscale regularity motivates a hybrid discretization framework that combines localized real-space discretizations in atomic patches with plane waves in the interstitial region. In this work, we employ tensor-product B-splines in the atomic patches and couple the two approximation spaces through a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin formulation, yielding the isogeometric-plane wave (IGA-PW) method. To efficiently evaluate the restricted plane wave integrals, we develop a combined fast Fourier transform and Chebyshev correction strategy. We also construct a trace-block DG preconditioner to alleviate the conditioning deterioration caused by the SIPG penalty terms and accelerate the iterative eigensolver. In addition, we establish {\it a priori} error estimates for the corresponding linear eigenvalue problem, showing algebraic convergence near the nuclei and superalgebraic convergence in the interstitial region. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid discontinuous Galerkin method combining B-splines and plane waves for periodic full-potential electronic structure calculations.
motivation: To efficiently handle the multiscale regularity in full-potential electronic structure calculations where orbitals have cusp behavior near nuclei and are smooth in the interstitial region.
method: A hybrid discretization using tensor-product B-splines in atomic patches and plane waves in the interstitial region, coupled via a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin formulation, with fast Fourier transform and Chebyshev correction for integral evaluation and a trace-block DG preconditioner.
result: The method achieves algebraic convergence near nuclei and superalgebraic convergence in the interstitial region, demonstrated through numerical experiments.
conclusion: The IGA-PW method provides an accurate and efficient approach for periodic electronic structure calculations, with potential for further development in computational materials science.

title: Shifted Matrix-Sign Reflectors For Prescribed-Index Eigenspace Reflection
authors: Jin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral projectors and the reflectors derived from them are basic objects in numerical linear algebra. This paper studies the prescribed-index reflector I-2P_k, where P_k is the spectral projector associated with the first k eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix. If a shift s lies in the target spectral gap, then this reflector is exactly the shifted matrix sign sign(H-sI). The exact identity is elementary, but its algorithmic consequences are not: all admissible shifts give the same exact reflector, while finite-step sign filters can have very different errors. We analyze odd sign-preserving spectral filters, prove local inheritance and discrete stability for the induced reflector iterations, derive a gap-dependent Newton-Schulz operator bound, and give deterministic admissibility certificates for inexact and reused shifts. The analysis identifies the shifted spectral margin as the quantity controlling finite-step reflector accuracy and explains why the midpoint shift is the natural default. Numerical experiments separate the matrix-function issues from the outer saddle-search dynamics: controlled spectra verify the margin predictions, low-dimensional tests distinguish shifted signs from raw signs, target-index scans probe non-small k, and Allen-Cahn and dense timing tests identify the regimes in which full-matrix sign filters are useful and the stiff regimes in which stronger sign engines are needed.
tldr: This paper studies shifted matrix-sign reflectors for eigenspace reflection in numerical linear algebra, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To analyze the accuracy and stability of finite-step sign filters for computing prescribed-index reflectors, which are basic objects in numerical linear algebra.
method: Theoretical analysis of odd sign-preserving spectral filters, proving local inheritance and discrete stability, and deriving gap-dependent Newton-Schulz operator bounds.
result: The shifted spectral margin controls finite-step reflector accuracy; the midpoint shift is the natural default; numerical experiments verify margin predictions and distinguish shifted signs from raw signs.
conclusion: The analysis provides deterministic admissibility certificates for inexact shifts and identifies regimes where full-matrix sign filters are useful or where stronger sign engines are needed.

title: IV-Net: A Neural Network For Elliptic PDEs With Random And Highly Varying Coefficients
authors: George Biros Shan Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a novel neural operator architecture designed to approximate solutions of linear elliptic partial differential equations with high-contrast, spatially varying coefficients. The network, termed the Iterated V-shaped Net (IV-Net), realizes a mapping from the input coefficients and righthand side to the corresponding solution field. The architecture of IV-Net is informed by, and closely resembles, a V-cycle multigrid solver. The IV-Net model is parameterized via convolutional layers defined in the physical domain. For coercive problems with highly heterogeneous coefficients, the proposed network exhibits superior performance relative to a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) approach and several existing neural operator architectures. For low-frequency oscillatory Helmholtz problems with smooth coefficients, its performance is similar to that of a Fourier neural operator. We analyze the approximation error and convergence behavior of IV-Net, its data efficiency, and its dependence on the underlying discretization mesh. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the architecture through a series of numerical experiments, including applications to uncertainty quantification, inverse problems, and prediction of quantities of interest.
tldr: IV-Net is a neural operator for solving elliptic PDEs with random coefficients, inspired by multigrid methods.
motivation: To develop a neural network that efficiently approximates solutions to elliptic PDEs with high-contrast coefficients, outperforming existing methods.
method: The architecture mimics a V-cycle multigrid solver using convolutional layers in the physical domain.
result: IV-Net shows superior performance over POD and other neural operators for heterogeneous coefficients, and matches Fourier neural operators for Helmholtz problems.
conclusion: The method is effective for uncertainty quantification and inverse problems, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Simulation Of Gaussian Random Fields On Surfaces Using The Isogeometric Finite Element Method
authors: Helmut Harbrecht, Florian Sonderegger, Remo von Rickenbach
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We are concerned with the fast simulation of random fields on closed surfaces in [MATH] which are generated by the (Whittle-) Mat\'ern class of covariance functions. To this end, we solve the underlying fractional stochastic partial differential equation with additive white noise by using an isogeometric finite element method on the surface in combination with the Balakrishnan integral representation of the solution. The solution of the underlying linear system of equations is performed by means of a geometric multigrid method that naturally underlies the isogeometric approach. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the approach.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for simulating Gaussian random fields on surfaces using isogeometric finite elements and multigrid solvers.
motivation: Efficient simulation of random fields on surfaces is needed in geostatistics, computer graphics, and uncertainty quantification.
method: The authors solve a fractional SPDE with additive white noise via an isogeometric FEM on surfaces, using the Balakrishnan integral representation and a geometric multigrid method.
result: Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach for generating Matérn random fields on closed surfaces.
conclusion: The method provides a fast and accurate way to simulate Gaussian random fields on surfaces, with potential applications in various fields requiring random field generation.

title: Verifiable Secure Aggregation Via Dual Servers With Linear Tags In Federated Learning
authors: Yufei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training by aggregating local updates without requiring raw data sharing. However, prior studies have shown that servers can exploit gradient inversion to compromise user privacy or manipulate aggregation results, undermining the utility of the global model. To address these concerns, we propose a secure and verifiable aggregation scheme with lightweight cryptographic primitives for FL. Our method leverages pseudo-random functions (PRFs) and a non-colluding dual-server architecture to achieve secure aggregation with mutual server verification, while maintaining communication overhead comparable to plaintext aggregation and a constant verification tag size. Crucially, it preserves user privacy and achieves end-to-end secure aggregation with verification. Moreover, our scheme significantly reduces both user computation and verification overhead, making it suitable for FL with a large number of participants. For instance, with an input dimension of 20K, user computation time is reduced to 18 ms, approximately 7[MATH] faster than OPSA, while verification time decreases to 9.5 ms, approximately 2.4[MATH] faster than OPSA.
tldr: This paper proposes a secure and verifiable aggregation scheme for federated learning using dual servers and linear tags, focusing on privacy and efficiency.
motivation: Existing federated learning schemes are vulnerable to gradient inversion attacks and malicious server manipulation, compromising user privacy and model utility.
method: The scheme employs pseudo-random functions and a non-colluding dual-server architecture to achieve secure aggregation with mutual server verification, while keeping communication overhead comparable to plaintext aggregation and constant verification tag size.
result: The scheme significantly reduces user computation and verification overhead; for input dimension 20K, user computation time is 18 ms (7× faster than OPSA) and verification time is 9.5 ms (2.4× faster than OPSA).
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides end-to-end secure aggregation with verification, making it suitable for large-scale federated learning, though its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Microbenchmarking Cloud Cryptographic Workloads For Privacy-Preserving Healthcare IoT
authors: Jeremiah L. Webb, Laxima Niure Kandel, Deepti Gupta, Lavanya Elluri
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptographic operations are an essential component of cloud security architectures; their comprehensive performance characterization across different cloud services, hardware architectures, and programming language implementations remains unknown. Specifically, healthcare IoT devices are highly vulnerable and frequently targeted, yet the cryptographic performance trade offs in their cloud security architectures remain poorly understood. This research presents an extensive microbenchmark study evaluating the performance of core cryptographic workloads, including SHA HMAC generation, AES encryption, decryption, Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) signature generation and verification, and RSA encryption, decryption, across Function as a Service (FaaS) integrated with Key Management Services (KMS) from Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure. We evaluate FaaS platforms using Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances and Azure Virtual Machines, specifically using burst optimized instance types to analyze performance under typical cloud workload patterns. The benchmark encompasses a comprehensive multi dimensional analysis spanning two CPU architectures (x86 64 and Arm64), six widely adopted programming languages (Rust, Go, Python, Java, C#, and TypeScript), multiple memory allocation configurations, and diverse instance types to capture the complex interplay between these factors. This study identifies optimal configurations for cryptographic workloads in FaaS environments, improving performance and cost efficiency while enabling secure and timely data protection for healthcare IoT applications.
tldr: This paper benchmarks cryptographic workloads on cloud FaaS platforms for healthcare IoT, but does not address quantum computing, information thermodynamics, or quantum foundations.
motivation: Healthcare IoT devices are vulnerable, and the performance of cryptographic operations across cloud services, hardware, and languages is poorly understood.
method: Microbenchmarking of SHA, AES, ECC, and RSA on AWS and Azure FaaS with different CPU architectures, languages, and memory configurations.
result: Identified optimal configurations for cryptographic workloads in FaaS environments, improving performance and cost efficiency.
conclusion: The study provides guidance for secure and timely data protection in healthcare IoT, but is not relevant to quantum information science.

title: Deep-Research Agents Can Be Poisoned Via User-Generated Content
authors: Tingwei Zhang, Harold Triedman, Vitaly Shmatikov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep-research agents, i.e., systems that rely on multi-agent pipelines to iteratively retrieve, synthesize, and cite Web content in order to produce structured reports, are rapidly replacing traditional search for both routine and complex information needs. These agents issue many related queries during a single research session. We show that for many common search topics, they repeatedly retrieve the same user-generated content (UGC) pages from platforms such as Reddit and Wikipedia. Next, we argue that this retrieval overlap creates a concentrated attack surface: an adversary who appends a short, crafted text to a single, frequently retrieved UGC page can cause the agent to cite attacker-chosen content and promote attacker-chosen entities across many related queries. We evaluate this attack on three representative deep-research systems (STORM, Co-STORM, and OmniThink) across multiple query clusters. We also study defenses at different stages of the pipeline, including source-level filtering and output-based detection. Our findings highlight a fundamental vulnerability in how deep-research agents retrieve and integrate web content.
tldr: This paper shows that deep-research agents can be poisoned by appending crafted text to frequently retrieved user-generated content pages, causing them to cite attacker-chosen content.
motivation: Deep-research agents are increasingly used for information retrieval, but their reliance on repeated retrieval of the same UGC pages creates a vulnerability that could be exploited.
method: The authors identify frequently retrieved UGC pages for common search topics, then append short crafted text to those pages and evaluate the impact on three deep-research systems (STORM, Co-STORM, OmniThink) across multiple query clusters.
result: An adversary can cause the agent to cite attacker-chosen content and promote attacker-chosen entities across many related queries. Defenses at different pipeline stages are studied but not fully effective.
conclusion: The findings highlight a fundamental vulnerability in how deep-research agents retrieve and integrate web content, suggesting the need for more robust defenses.

title: Reframing Llm Agent Security As An Agent-Human Interaction Problem
authors: Peiran Wang, Ying Li, Yuan Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that LLM agent security is fundamentally an agent-human interaction (AHI) problem, not a purely algorithmic one. To substantiate this position, we conduct a systematic analysis of 59 academic papers, 21 production agent systems, and 26 security plugins as of April 2026. Our analysis reveals a striking pattern: the three widely deployed human-centric security mechanisms (policy specification, runtime approval, and scope configuration) dominate industry practice, each adopted by at least 14 of 21 systems (14, 15, and 16, respectively), while the categories most heavily studied in academia (intent anchoring and trust labeling) see zero production deployment. Yet current human participation mechanisms are far from satisfactory: they suffer from a fundamental trade-off between cognitive burden and security guarantees, leaving users caught between approval fatigue and uncontrolled agent autonomy. We make three contributions. First, through a systematic comparison of LLM-based and human-based intent alignment, we argue that human participation in agent security decisions is indispensable given current capabilities. Second, we quantify a pronounced industry-academia mismatch: the security mechanisms that practitioners actually deploy receive scant research attention, while the approaches that researchers favor remain undeployed. Third, we propose a three-direction research agenda and call for AHI security to be recognized as a first-class research citizen, one that demands its own design principles, evaluation methods, and theoretical foundations.
tldr: This paper argues that LLM agent security is fundamentally an agent-human interaction problem, not a purely algorithmic one, and identifies a mismatch between academic research and industry practice.
motivation: To address the gap between academic research on LLM agent security and the actual deployment of human-centric security mechanisms in industry.
method: Systematic analysis of 59 academic papers, 21 production agent systems, and 26 security plugins as of April 2026.
result: Human-centric mechanisms (policy specification, runtime approval, scope configuration) dominate industry but are understudied academically; academic favorites (intent anchoring, trust labeling) see zero deployment.
conclusion: Calls for recognizing agent-human interaction security as a first-class research area with its own design principles and evaluation methods.

title: Five Queries Are Enough: Query-Efficient And Surrogate-Free Membership Inference Attacks On Rag Via Entailment
authors: Nguyen Linh Bao Nguyen, Wanlun Ma, Viet Vo, Alsharif Abuadbba, Minghong Fang, Jun Zhang, Yang Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become central to large language model (LLM) deployments, grounding responses in enterprise or proprietary data to reduce hallucinations. However, this design introduces a new privacy risk: model outputs may signal the presence of specific documents in the retrieval corpus, enabling membership inference attacks (MIAs) that leak sensitive information. Existing MIAs are feasible, but they often rely on easily detected templated queries or require many non-templated yet costly and repetitive queries, limiting practicality. We ask: Can an adversary launch a limited-budget, surrogate-free, stealthy, and defense-agnostic membership inference attack using non-templated queries? We present MEntA (Membership Entailment Attack), a query-efficient MIA that leverages natural-language entailment to maximize information gained per query. By asking low-cost, broad, information-seeking questions and measuring entailment between model responses and candidate documents, MEntA eliminates the need for costly shadow models and large query budgets. Across NFCorpus, SCIDOCS, and TREC-COVID, MEntA achieves up to 0.991 AUC with only 5 queries, outperforming prior methods by 0.20 to 0.50 AUC under equivalent conditions. It remains effective under state-of-the-art (SOTA) RAG defenses, while current detectors either miss MEntA or flag benign queries at high rates. Regarding cost, MEntA reduces total attack cost by up to 65 [MATH] lower compared to SOTA attacks under the same attack setting. Our findings expose the feasibility of realistic, low-cost privacy leakage in RAG systems and highlight the urgent need for privacy-aware retrieval and defense mechanisms.
tldr: This paper presents a query-efficient membership inference attack on RAG systems using entailment, achieving high AUC with only five queries.
motivation: Existing membership inference attacks on RAG systems are either easily detected or require many queries; the authors aim to develop a stealthy, low-cost attack.
method: The attack, MEntA, uses natural-language entailment to measure the relationship between model responses and candidate documents, requiring only a few broad queries without shadow models.
result: MEntA achieves up to 0.991 AUC with only five queries on three datasets, outperforming prior methods by 0.20-0.50 AUC, and remains effective against state-of-the-art defenses.
conclusion: The work exposes realistic privacy leakage risks in RAG systems and calls for privacy-aware retrieval and defense mechanisms.

title: Steering Beyond The Support: Adversarial Training On Unsupervised Jailbroken Activation Simulation
authors: Luoyu Chen, Weiqi Wang, Zhiyi Tian, Chenhan Zhang, Feng Wu, Jianhuan Huang, Ahmed Asiri, Shui Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jailbreak prompts can trigger harmful completions on aligned LLMs, In accordance, safety steering has been proposed: test-time activation interventions that steer jailbreak activations to trigger refusal while preserving benign utility. However, existing steering methods are fundamentally supervised and tied to a static, limited training set, whereas real jailbreaks evolve and are often out-of-distributed from the training set, leading to failures on unseen attacks. In this paper, we tackle the failure on unseen jailbreaks problem, base on unsupervised latent direction discovery. We propose a bi-level adversarial training framework for zero-shot jailbreak defense. In the inner step, we simulate diverse jail-broken activations by extrapolating from refusal-state harmful-request activations via unsupervised latent direction discovery, which expands the coverage of real jailbreak activation subspaces. In the outer step, we train a potential-induced steering field to push these adversarial jailbroken states into refusal regions while keeping benign unchanged. Across three LLMs and six classical jailbreak families, our method achieves strong defense with attack success rates mostly below 5%, and rising subspace coverage throughout training helps explain the improved generalization.
tldr: This paper proposes an adversarial training framework for jailbreak defense in LLMs using unsupervised latent direction discovery.
motivation: Existing steering methods for LLM safety are supervised and fail on unseen jailbreak attacks.
method: A bi-level adversarial training framework that simulates diverse jailbroken activations via unsupervised latent direction discovery and trains a potential-induced steering field to push them into refusal regions.
result: Achieves strong defense with attack success rates mostly below 5% across three LLMs and six jailbreak families.
conclusion: The method improves generalization to unseen jailbreaks, with rising subspace coverage explaining the improved defense.

title: AI-Driven Adaptive Adversaries And The Erosion Of Cryptographic Trust In Public Key Systems
authors: Petar Radanliev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper examines the erosion of Public Key Cryptography (PKC) security under adaptive adversarial optimisation driven by artificial intelligence. The problem addressed is the growing mismatch between algorithm-centric cryptographic security models and operational attack realities, where adversaries exploit implementation-level observability rather than breaking cryptographic primitives.
tldr: This paper discusses AI-driven adaptive attacks on public key cryptography, focusing on implementation-level vulnerabilities rather than breaking cryptographic primitives.
motivation: To address the mismatch between theoretical cryptographic security models and real-world attacks that exploit implementation observability.
method: Conceptual analysis of adaptive adversarial optimization using AI, likely with examples or case studies of attack scenarios.
result: The paper argues that AI enables adaptive adversaries to erode trust in public key systems by exploiting side-channel information and implementation weaknesses.
conclusion: Implications for cryptographic security: need for new models that account for AI-driven adaptive threats; future work may involve developing countermeasures.

title: Memory-Induced Tool-Drift In Llm Agents
authors: Mahavir Dabas, Jihyun Jeong, Ming Jin, Ruoxi Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern LLM agents combine long-term memory for personalization with tool-calling interfaces for taking actions in the world -- a combination underpinning contemporary production systems. We study a previously unexamined failure of this combination: when personality-driven biases stored in memory (cost-consciousness, impatience, risk tolerance, etc.) silently affect tool calls in contexts where they are not applicable. We call this memory-induced tool-drift and operationalize it through MEMDRIFT, a benchmark of 105 scenarios spanning five bias dimensions and seven professional domains, generated through an automated adversarial pipeline. Across seven frontier models -- including those with extended reasoning -- biased memories raise deflection scores (a judge-scored measure of parameter deviation from unbiased baselines) by up to [MATH] points on a 1--5 scale. Tool-drift persists when memory management is handled by three production memory architectures. The phenomenon affects real-world tools: scanning 6{,}062 tools across 288 verified MCP servers, we flag 608 with susceptible parameters and confirm tool-drift on a validated subset. Mechanistically, biased memories act as implicit steering vectors, pushing activations along the same latent directions as explicit behavioral instructions. They also redistribute attention from task-relevant context toward memory entries with surface-level keyword overlap to the target parameter. Standard defenses -- prompt-based relevance instructions and memory filters -- reduce drift but do not eliminate it. As agents take increasingly consequential actions on a user's behalf, memory-induced tool-drift represents a systematic vulnerability that current safeguards do not address, motivating dedicated defenses at the intersection of memory management and tool-call generation.
tldr: This paper identifies and benchmarks a failure mode in LLM agents where biased long-term memory causes unintended deviations in tool-call parameters, termed memory-induced tool-drift.
motivation: To uncover and characterize a previously unexamined vulnerability in LLM agents that combine long-term memory with tool-calling, which could lead to unsafe or biased actions.
method: The authors develop MEMDRIFT, a benchmark of 105 scenarios across five bias dimensions and seven domains, generated via an automated adversarial pipeline. They test seven frontier models and three memory architectures, and scan 6,062 tools from MCP servers to identify susceptible parameters.
result: Biased memories increase deflection scores by up to 2.5 points on a 1-5 scale. Tool-drift persists across memory architectures, and biased memories act as implicit steering vectors, redistributing attention toward memory entries with surface-level keyword overlap.
conclusion: Memory-induced tool-drift is a systematic vulnerability not addressed by current safeguards, motivating dedicated defenses at the intersection of memory management and tool-call generation.

title: EnThM: Energy Theft Mitigation In Smart Grids Using Hierarchical Verification Of Metering Data
authors: Tapadyoti Banerjee, Pabitra Mitra, Dipanwita Roy Chowdhury
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advent of digital technologies has revolutionized traditional power distribution networks, transforming them into smart grids that are more reliable, efficient, and sustainable. Despite these advancements, electricity theft remains a significant threat to the effective operation of large electrical networks. To address this issue, we propose EnThM, a lightweight and communication-efficient scheme for real-time mitigation of power theft in smart grid systems. Our approach uses the hierarchical structure of the smart grid infrastructure to verify the authenticity of the metering data at multiple levels of the power distribution network. Our work focuses primarily on issues related to cryptographic security. The verification process involves statistically modeling the cumulative averages of the power usage data and applying rule-based checks on the aggregated power consumption at each level, while accounting for seasonal and daily consumption variations. The proposed method has been tested on benchmark consumption data, yielding high accuracy, efficient implementation, and real-time applicability.
tldr: EnThM proposes a lightweight hierarchical verification scheme for detecting energy theft in smart grids using statistical modeling and rule-based checks.
motivation: Electricity theft remains a major threat to smart grid operations, and existing solutions may be too heavy or communication-intensive.
method: The scheme uses hierarchical verification of metering data at multiple levels, statistically modeling cumulative averages and applying rule-based checks that account for seasonal and daily variations.
result: Tested on benchmark consumption data, the method achieves high accuracy, efficient implementation, and real-time applicability.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical solution for real-time energy theft mitigation, but its cryptographic security focus and lack of quantum or thermodynamic aspects limit relevance to the user's interests.

title: Integrated Sensing, Communication, And Computing For Nr-v2x: A Cross-Layer Resource Allocation Framework Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: T. G. Venkatesh Indulekha K. P.
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC) is emerging as a unified design paradigm for future vehicular networks that require joint environment perception, safety-critical information exchange, and latency-sensitive task processing. In New Radio Vehicle-to-Everything (NR-V2X) Mode 2, autonomous resource selection is performed through sensing-based semi-persistent scheduling (SB-SPS), which is effective for distributed communication resource reservation but does not explicitly consider sensing-resource demand, task-induced computation workload, and the additional latency introduced by mobile edge computing (MEC) offloading. This paper develops multi-agent proximal policy optimization-based SB-SPS (MAPPO-SPS), an ISCC-aware cross-layer scheduler that jointly adapts SB-SPS reservation, radio-resource partitioning, and overflow-driven computation-offloading decisions at control epochs. The scheduling problem is formulated as a cooperative partially observable Markov game and solved using MAPPO with centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). Simulation results show that MAPPO-SPS achieves a balanced tradeoff among CRLB-based sensing accuracy, packet reception ratio (PRR), effective throughput, energy consumption, and end-to-end delay.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for integrated sensing, communication, and computation in vehicular networks, focusing on NR-V2X resource allocation.
motivation: To address the lack of joint optimization of sensing, communication, and computation in NR-V2X Mode 2, which traditionally only considers communication resource reservation.
method: Formulates the problem as a cooperative partially observable Markov game and solves it using multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) with centralized training and decentralized execution.
result: The proposed MAPPO-SPS scheduler achieves a balanced tradeoff among sensing accuracy, packet reception ratio, throughput, energy consumption, and end-to-end delay.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of ISCC-aware scheduling in vehicular networks, but its relevance to quantum information science is minimal.

title: Securing High-Performance Data Transfers: Implementing Aes Encryption In Rdma Systems
authors: Erik B{\aa}ngsbo, Zakaria Hersi, Anna Benktson, Stefan Holmgren, Romaric Duvignau
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) is a key enabler of high-performance systems, offering low latency, high throughput, and reduced CPU overhead by allowing direct memory-to-memory transfers between machines. However, its design bypasses traditional CPU-mediated security mechanisms, introducing critical vulnerabilities in untrusted environments. This work explores the integration of RDMA and AES-128 encryption to secure data transfers without compromising performance. We implement encryption directly within the data plane of a programmable Tofino switch using the P4 programming language. By offloading encryption from the CPU to the switch, our design preserves RDMA's performance benefits while addressing its security shortcomings. Experimental results show that the system achieves throughput of 0.37 Gbps for 16-byte packets, 0.76 Gbps for 32-byte packets, 1.83 Gbps for 64-byte packets, and 1.9 Gbps for 128-byte packets. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of secure, high-throughput RDMA communication using programmable network hardware.
tldr: This paper implements AES-128 encryption in the data plane of a programmable Tofino switch to secure RDMA data transfers without compromising performance.
motivation: RDMA bypasses traditional CPU-mediated security, introducing vulnerabilities in untrusted environments. The research aims to secure RDMA transfers while preserving its performance benefits.
method: The authors implement AES-128 encryption directly within the data plane of a programmable Tofino switch using the P4 programming language, offloading encryption from the CPU to the switch.
result: The system achieves throughput of 0.37 Gbps for 16-byte packets, 0.76 Gbps for 32-byte packets, 1.83 Gbps for 64-byte packets, and 1.9 Gbps for 128-byte packets.
conclusion: The results demonstrate the feasibility of secure, high-throughput RDMA communication using programmable network hardware, but the paper does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Design Of Apsk Constellations Approaching The Communication-Sensing Pareto Boundary For Isac
authors: Yujie Shao, Min Qiu, Ming-Chun Lee, Yu-Chih Huang, Jinhong Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a semi-analytical amplitude phase shift keying (APSK) signaling framework for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), focusing on i.i.d. uniform discrete input distributions for practicality and analytical tractability. First, we establish APSK design criteria in which communication performance is measured by the gap to capacity and linked to the minimum Euclidean distance, while sensing performance is characterized by the symbol-energy variance. Based on these criteria, we propose a family of APSK constellations whose key parameters follow explicit scaling laws. Then we prove that this design achieves a constant gap to capacity independent of the signal-to-noise ratio. Building upon this foundation, we further construct a parametric APSK family that bridges the communication-optimal and sensing-optimal designs, with the communication and sensing (C&S) tradeoff controlled by the number of rings and energy allocation among rings. Simulation results show that the proposed APSK achieves C&S performance very close to the Pareto boundary achieved with time-independent, circularly symmetric, and otherwise unconstrained continuous input distributions.
tldr: This paper designs APSK constellations for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) to approach the Pareto boundary of communication-sensing tradeoff.
motivation: To achieve optimal tradeoff between communication and sensing performance in ISAC systems using practical discrete input distributions.
method: Semi-analytical framework with APSK constellations; communication performance linked to minimum Euclidean distance, sensing performance to symbol-energy variance; parametric family bridging communication-optimal and sensing-optimal designs.
result: Proposed APSK achieves constant gap to capacity and performance close to the Pareto boundary of continuous input distributions.
conclusion: The design provides a practical signaling scheme for ISAC with near-optimal tradeoff, but relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Eliminating Blind Spots From Wireless Network By Metasurface: A Blind Approach
authors: Wenhai Lai, Mingxiao Li, Kaiming Shen, Liyao Xiang, Zhi-Quan Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying metasurfaces (MTSs) to eliminate wireless blind spots requires jointly determining the physical placement of MTSs and the meta-atom phase shifts. Existing methods typically rely on explicit channel estimation, which incurs prohibitive overhead and is often intractable in real-world networks. To sidestep this bottleneck, we propose RFZero, a channel-state-information (CSI)-free deployment paradigm. Instead of estimating channels, RFZero extracts macro-environmental features from visual photos to guide MTS placement, and leverages reference signal received power (RSRP) feedback for dynamic phase-shift optimization. Most importantly, RFZero operates independently of base stations, thereby enabling seamless plug-and-play implementation. Real-world field tests confirm that RFZero completely eliminates all blind spots in a [MATH] indoor area using just a pair of [MATH] MTSs.
tldr: This paper proposes a CSI-free metasurface deployment method to eliminate wireless blind spots using visual features and RSRP feedback.
motivation: Existing metasurface deployment methods rely on explicit channel estimation, which is impractical in real-world networks due to high overhead.
method: RFZero extracts macro-environmental features from visual photos to guide MTS placement and uses RSRP feedback for dynamic phase-shift optimization, operating independently of base stations.
result: Real-world tests show that RFZero completely eliminates all blind spots in a 100m² indoor area using just two MTSs.
conclusion: The approach enables plug-and-play metasurface deployment without channel estimation, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Pre-Characterization Of Electromagnetic Side-Channel Leakage Using Publicly Available Information: A Case Study On E-Voting Interfaces
authors: Leonardo Teodoro, Kemuel L. Vieira, Saulo Queiroz
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the interface of the Brazilian e-Voting Machine (BVM) in the context of electromagnetic side-channel threats commonly referred to as TEMPEST attacks. In a TEMPEST attack against video displays, an eavesdropper uses Software-Defined Radios (SDRs) to recover sensitive information by intercepting electromagnetic emanations generated during video signal transmission. We emulate the BVM using a VGA monitor by leveraging publicly available information disclosed by the electoral authority, including technical specifications, operational rules of the system, and the official BVM interface. Based on this setup, we investigate whether the BVM interface gives rise to a distinctive spectral signature observable through its unintended electromagnetic emissions. Our findings show that design characteristics relevant to a nationwide electoral process -- such as high image contrast, minimal on-screen information, and the prohibition of other electronic devices within the polling station -- result in a simple and highly distinctive spectral signature that can be observed even through a wall in our experiments. Although our experiments do not involve actual BVM hardware, the results raise concerns regarding the system's susceptibility to TEMPEST attacks and highlight the need for further research on protective countermeasures. In this context, our findings may support the design of automatic jammers capable of adaptively targeting compromising frequencies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study investigating TEMPEST attacks in the context of an electronic voting system officially adopted by a country.
tldr: This paper investigates electromagnetic side-channel leakage (TEMPEST attacks) from the interface of a Brazilian e-voting machine using publicly available information and a VGA monitor emulation.
motivation: To assess the vulnerability of the Brazilian e-Voting Machine to TEMPEST attacks, which could compromise vote secrecy, and to inform the design of countermeasures.
method: The authors emulated the BVM interface using a VGA monitor based on publicly available specifications, then used software-defined radios to capture electromagnetic emanations and analyze spectral signatures.
result: The BVM interface produces a simple and highly distinctive spectral signature observable even through a wall, indicating susceptibility to TEMPEST attacks.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for protective countermeasures, such as adaptive jammers, and call for further research on TEMPEST attacks in electronic voting systems.

title: Decoupling Reentrancy Protection From Smart Contract Implementation Logic
authors: Wojciech Golab Shashank Joshi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.25207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reentrancy attacks remain a persistent threat to decentralized applications (DApps), with malicious actors siphoning around 80M USD from the DApp ecosystem last year by exploiting EVM's inter-contract message-passing semantics. Existing research focuses primarily on detection, relying on known attack patterns, and fails to provide deployable solutions that eliminate the vulnerability. Traditional reentrancy guards are similarly limited, offering incomplete coverage across attack variations and lacking robustness against complex DApp interactions. In this paper, we introduce Sentinel, a novel proxy-based approach that mitigates reentrancy vulnerabilities in a type-agnostic way by integrating reentrancy logic directly into the proxy layer, intercepting all calls to the underlying implementation contract. Key features include a dual-mode operational system offering both a gas-optimized internal guard and a high-security external lock registry for cross-contract reentrancy prevention. The proxy also intelligently handles static calls, enabling safe view-function execution while protecting against Read-Only Reentrancy (ROR) attacks. Through rigorous evaluation on a dataset of 70 vulnerable smart contracts, Sentinel achieves 100% security coverage across four major reentrancy attack categories, outperforming existing solutions by over 40%.
tldr: This paper introduces Sentinel, a proxy-based reentrancy protection mechanism for Ethereum smart contracts, achieving 100% coverage across four attack categories.
motivation: Reentrancy attacks continue to cause significant financial losses in DApps, and existing solutions lack comprehensive coverage and deployability.
method: Sentinel integrates reentrancy logic into a proxy layer that intercepts all calls to the implementation contract, featuring a dual-mode system with an internal guard and an external lock registry, plus intelligent handling of static calls.
result: Evaluation on 70 vulnerable contracts shows 100% security coverage across four major reentrancy attack categories, outperforming existing solutions by over 40%.
conclusion: The approach provides a deployable, type-agnostic solution for reentrancy protection, with potential for broader adoption in smart contract security.

title: Long Memory In Intrinsically Dynamic Factor Models
authors: Qin Wen (stern School, New York University), Clifford M. Hurvich
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the generalized dynamic factor model in a long-memory setting. Unlike most recent work, which assumes a finite-dimensional factor space and short memory, our framework allows the factor space to be infinite-dimensional and the common components to exhibit long memory. We employ the two-sided estimation method of Forni, Hallin, Lippi and Reichlin (2000, Review of Economics and Statistics) to recover the common component. The long memory structure of the common component poses a challenge, as it introduces unboundedness/discontinuity in the spectral density. We address this issue by leveraging two key facts: First, the estimated operator is a projection onto the leading eigenspace and thus the eigengap provides an intrinsic scaling that partially mitigates the blow-up. Second, we perform most of our estimation in [MATH]-norm, rather than pointwise. Experimental results are presented to provide evidence supporting the theory, as well as potential improvements to it.
tldr: This paper studies long memory in generalized dynamic factor models, a topic in econometrics and time series analysis, with no connection to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.
motivation: To extend dynamic factor models to accommodate infinite-dimensional factor spaces and long memory common components, addressing challenges from unbounded spectral densities.
method: Uses two-sided estimation from Forni et al. (2000) and leverages eigengap scaling and L2-norm estimation to handle spectral density blow-up.
result: Theoretical results show that the eigengap provides intrinsic scaling to mitigate blow-up, and L2-norm estimation is effective; experimental evidence supports the theory.
conclusion: The work advances time series econometrics but has no implications for the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Petrol Station Game: The Regional Average Price. A Mean Field Analysis
authors: Fabio Bagagiolo, Federico Pontiroli, Ivan Roman\`o
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In January 2023, the obligation for petrol stations to display the average fuel price calculated on a regional basis was introduced by the Italian Government. A mean field game model is here proposed to describe the evolution of the fuel price. In particular, each petrol station decides its own price, for the next day, taking account of an estimate of the average price, to be communicated by the Local Authority. The existence and the evolution of a mean field equilibrium are analytically investigated. Some simulations are compared with real data from the Autonomous Province of Trento, Italy.
tldr: This paper applies mean field game theory to model fuel price dynamics in Italian petrol stations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To analyze the effect of a new Italian regulation requiring petrol stations to display regional average fuel prices.
method: Mean field game model where each station sets its price based on an estimate of the regional average, with analytical investigation of equilibrium existence and evolution.
result: Existence and evolution of a mean field equilibrium are analytically shown; simulations are compared with real data from Trento.
conclusion: The model captures price dynamics under the regulation, with potential for policy insights, but no relevance to quantum research.

title: On Permutation Groups Of Cyclic Codes Over Finite Fields
authors: Junjie Huang, Jicheng Ma, Chang-An Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The permutation groups of cyclic codes are widely applicable in determining the weight distribution of codes, decoding theory and various other areas. In this paper, by employing two distinct matrix representations, we can relate cyclic codes with very long lengths and special generator polynomials to those with prime lengths. Consequently, we mainly determine the permutation groups of certain cyclic codes over [MATH] with lengths [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH] and special generator polynomials where [MATH] is a positive integer and [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH] are distinct prime numbers. For length [MATH], we manage to provide the permutation groups of cyclic codes with generator polynomials [MATH](the [MATH]-th cyclotomic polynomial) or others, which seems to be the first work about permutation groups of cyclic codes with generator polynomials that are factors of [MATH] but not factors of [MATH].
tldr: This paper determines permutation groups of cyclic codes over finite fields with specific lengths and generator polynomials.
motivation: To understand the structure of cyclic codes and their permutation groups, which are useful for weight distribution and decoding.
method: Uses two distinct matrix representations to relate long cyclic codes to prime-length codes, then analyzes permutation groups for lengths n = p^e, p^e q, p^e q r with special generator polynomials.
result: Determines permutation groups for cyclic codes with generator polynomials including the p^e-th cyclotomic polynomial, providing first results for codes where generator factors x^{p^e}-1 but not x^p-1.
conclusion: Extends knowledge of permutation groups to new classes of cyclic codes, with potential applications in coding theory.

title: On Exotic Rationally Integrable Planar Dual Billiards I. Complex Geometry And Type Of Dynamics
authors: Alexey Glutsyuk
abstract: ArXiv:2605.24434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A planar dual billiard is a planar curve [MATH] equipped with a family [MATH] of projective involutions of the projective lines [MATH] tangent to [MATH] at [MATH] that fix [MATH]. A dual billiard is called rationally integrable, if there exists a rational function [MATH] of two variables (called first integral) whose restriction to each tangent line [MATH] is [MATH]-invariant. In the previous author's paper it was shown that rationally integrable dual billiards exist only on conics punctured at [MATH] points, [MATH]. Their classification given there includes standard examples with quadratic integrals, defined by conical pencils, and an infinite family of exotic examples with minimal degree of integrals being any even number greater than two. In the present paper we study a question stated by Dmitry Treschev on dynamics and conservation laws in the exotic examples. We study the dynamics acting on the two-dimensional phase space: the complex algebraic surface consisting of pairs [MATH], where [MATH], [MATH] and the line [MATH] is tangent to [MATH] at [MATH]. We show that the phase space is fibered by invariant algebraic curves along which [MATH] lies in a level curve of the integral of the dual billiard. For each example we find the type of a generic level curve of the integral and of the corresponding fiber. We show that a generic level curve is rational in most of examples and elliptic in two examples. We present formulas for an invariant area form on the phase space and for invariant holomorphic differentials on invariant curves. This yields a formula for holomorphic differentials on the elliplic level curves of the integral.
tldr: This paper classifies exotic rationally integrable planar dual billiards and studies their dynamics, focusing on complex geometry and invariant curves.
motivation: To understand the dynamics and conservation laws in exotic dual billiards beyond standard quadratic integrals, as posed by Dmitry Treschev.
method: Complex algebraic geometry analysis of the phase space, fibering by invariant algebraic curves, and computation of generic level curve types.
